items.body:
Jason’s Sourdough, the UK’s number one sourdough brand, is partnering with mental health charity, Mind, to launch the Mindful Loaf.
Rolling out exclusively into Tesco from 31st August, Jason’s will donate 10p from every loaf sold to Mind.
The Mindful Loaf is made with pumpkin seeds which are a source of magnesium, which contributes to psychological function, as well as chia & flax seeds which are sources of omega-3 fatty acids, supporting normal brain function.
NEW! Jasons Sourdough’s Everyday Mindful Loaf
RRP: £2.80 (10p of every loaf sold donated to Mind)
Available at: 320 Tesco stores nationwide
Pack Weight: 580g
Mind, the leading mental health charity, believe that everyone should have access to mental health support that makes them feel seen, and starts on the day they ask for help. Through services like their helplines, website and online peer support community, together with the network of local Minds, rooted in communities across England and Wales, they offer frontline support when and where it’s needed.
Jason Geary, Master Baker at Jason’s Sourdough, says: “We’re proud to be kicking off our partnership with Mind with the launch of our new Mindful Loaf. With awareness around mental wellbeing continuing to grow, shoppers are increasingly conscious of how their diet contributes to this. That’s why we’ve developed a recipe with ingredients known for supporting brain function using our traditional baking heritage with the quality that aligns with our brand.
“As a company it felt important that we support the great work that Mind do, and as such 10p of each loaf sold will be donated directly to the charity.”
With more than a century of baking heritage, Geary’s, the family-run bakery behind Jason’s Sourdough, continues to balance time-honoured craft with a forward-thinking approach. Every Jason’s Sourdough product is made using a traditional slow fermentation process, delivering the signature tang and texture consumers know and love.
As demand for sourdough and premium bakery products continues to grow, Jason’s Sourdough remains steadfast in its commitment to quality. Just six years after launch, Jason’s has secured its place as the UK’s number one sourdough brand, and the third biggest supermarket bread brand[2], taking on established players and strengthening its influence across the bakery category.
This functional range launch builds on the simultaneous launch of the NEW Fibre Range, featuring the Every Day Seeded Fibre Rolls and a Seeded Fibre Loaf.

items.body:
VoCoVo, the retail communications specialist, today announces a partnership with home, leisure and garden retailer The Range, that will see its Series 5 (S5) Pro Headsets and Call Points rolled out across all 283 stores. This follows a successful one-store trial over the course of a year, which transformed efficiency, customer service and wellbeing.
As a result of the partnership, The Range colleagues will benefit from instant, hands-free communication through the headsets, replacing disruptive loudspeaker calls and reducing the need for colleagues to search the shop floor for one another.
The technology will help deliver faster, more responsive customer service by reducing waiting times at tills, service desks and across the shop floor. Colleagues will be empowered to contact managers and team members immediately for price and stock checks, quickly coordinate requests and assign tasks in real time, while two-way Call Points will allow customers to request assistance at the touch of a button and connect with available colleagues.
By connecting colleagues across the store, the VoCoVo Headsets will help create a calmer and more efficient working environment where colleagues spend less time chasing information and more time supporting customers, enabling The Range to deliver a more consistent experience at scale.
Over 12 months, the trial store saved 2,975 hours through reduced walking time and faster task completion. Colleagues also reduced the time taken to complete a price check by an average of 46 seconds using the headsets. Scaled across the full store network, these efficiencies are expected to save the retailer a significant number of hours each year.
A store manager at The Range said, “The headsets have made a hugely positive impact in-store for both colleagues and customers. Customer service has noticeably improved as queries are answered faster, stock checks are smoother and warehouse to shop floor communication is instant. This has already streamlined Deliveroo and Click & Collect, and I can see the headsets becoming invaluable during patio season. They’ve become essential to daily operations.
“The very impressive results already achieved in our store have laid the groundwork for much bigger savings across the store network. I can’t wait to see colleagues benefitting from the same technology.”
Beth Worrall, CEO, VoCoVo, said, “The initial trial with The Range has shown how they can achieve significant time and cost savings while maintaining outstanding service levels and the optimum in-store experience at the same time. We’re looking forward to working alongside the team to implement the technology across all its stores.”

items.body:
Fox’s Burton’s Companies (FBC) has been named as a UK distribution partner for the newly refreshed Jelly Belly range, bringing the iconic American gourmet jellybean brand back into major UK Grocery, for a first full nationwide grocery rollout.
Launching initially in Sainsbury’s from 5 September, the range will include four SKUs: Signature 10 Collection, Recipe Collection, Tropical Paradise Collection and Farmers’ Market Collection, bringing Jelly Belly’s distinctive flavour-led proposition to supermarket shelves in a new premium sharing format.
The move to distribute Jelly belly across major UK multiples capitalises on an existing 86% brand awareness among UK shoppers1, with purchase intent doubling among consumers who go on to try the product2. Previously available primarily through specialist confectionery stores, online and department stores, the move into grocery will significantly increase the brand’s accessibility, creating an exciting opportunity for retailers to convert existing recognition into trial and sales.
The launch also comes as shoppers increasingly look beyond traditional chocolate for more distinctive confectionery treats. Sugar confectionery purchase frequency is growing 2.8% year on year,3 creating an opportunity for retailers to encourage shoppers to trade up through more premium, flavour-led propositions.
The new range launches with a premium, resealable pouch format, designed to deliver stand-out on shelf and capitalise on sharing occasions.
Leading with the new tagline, “Bean Appétit,” the new range brings Jelly Belly’s long-standing legacy of gourmet flavour innovation to life, encouraging shoppers to “Explore the Art of Flavour” through four distinctive SKUs:
- Signature 10 Collection offers Jelly Belly fans a mix of the most-loved flavours, like Strawberry, Blueberry and Very Cherry.
- Recipe Collection is crafted for creativity, inviting shoppers to mix delicious flavours into gourmet flavour creations that take just like the real thing – two Green Apple and one Hot Cinnamon combine to take just like apple pie.
- Tropical Paradise Collection transports the consumer to a beach paradise, with exotic tastes, like Piña Colada and Mango.
- Farmers’ Market Collection is inspired by the charm of farm-fresh fruit, delivering gourmet flavours such as Peach, Green Apple and Juicy Pear. This SKU will remain exclusive to Sainsbury’s.
Speaking on the announcement, Jo Harwood, Chief Sales and Trade Marketing Officer at FBC, said: “Being named as UK distribution partner for Jelly Belly is a significant move for FBC. It’s a brand with genuine global fame and huge existing UK awareness, but no UK-wide grocery presence to match. We think shoppers are going to love discovering it properly for the first time with some exciting flavour combinations, and there’s huge opportunity for retailers to drive trial and incremental sales as a result.
“Unlike chocolate confectionery, we believe sugar confectionery is a massively under-premiumised market in the UK. Jelly Belly’s gourmet experience can unlock this potential, offering exciting trading up opportunities for retailers.”
Known as “The Original Gourmet Jelly Bean”, Jelly Belly built its reputation being “Flavour experts since 1976” through an extensive and artisanal manufacturing process. Each bean takes between 7 and 21 days to craft, and flavours are infused into both the centre and the shell of each bean, using high-quality ingredients. Individual beans are then checked for shape quality, with only perfect beans approved, and then individually stamped with the distinctive Jelly Belly logo.
FBC will back the launch with sampling at scale, putting the product directly in shoppers’ hands at Sainsbury’s from day one, alongside in-store activations to drive trial, awareness and overall category growth.
The 100g bags will RSP at £2.30 (promotional RSP £2), with further listings confirmed at Morrisons and Home Bargains rolling out from October 2026 and into 2027. A smaller 28g format has also been launched to unlock impulse and wholesale channels.

items.body:
Aldi is opening a new store every week throughout September, creating up to 120 new jobs across the four locations.
Following the opening of its new Balsall Common store near Solihull, Aldi will open a further three stores this September in Telford (Shropshire), Rayleigh (Essex) and Hoxton (East London), with up to 30 roles available at each location.
The openings form part of Aldi’s £370 million investment in new stores this year and its long-term ambition to operate 1,500 stores across the UK.
Jonathan Neale, managing director of National Real Estate at Aldi UK, said: “We know there are still communities across the country that want access to an Aldi store, and we’re working hard to bring our unbeatable value to more of them.
“Opening a new store every week throughout September demonstrates the pace of our expansion, while creating new jobs and bringing high-quality, affordable food to even more shoppers.”
Aldi stores opening across September are:
- Kenilworth Road, Balsall Common – 3rd September
- Waterloo Road, Ketley Point, Telford – 10th September
- Weir Retail Park, Rayleigh – 17th September
- Hackney Road, Hoxton – 24th September

items.body:
HECK! is expanding its popular high-protein chicken range with the launch of its first Cumberland Chicken Sausages, rolling into Tesco and Morrisons from mid-September.
The new six-pack SKU (340g, RRP £3.50) puts a lighter spin on the traditional Cumberland sausage, combining lean chicken with bold black pepper, fragrant sage and warming spices.
High in protein, gluten-free and naturally lower in fat than traditional pork sausages, the launch is designed to appeal to the growing number of shoppers looking for lighter, protein-rich alternatives without compromising on flavour.
HECK! co-founder Jamie Keeble said: “Cumberland is a UK household staple and one of Britain’s most popular sausage varieties, so it was an obvious choice for our latest chicken launch. We’ve kept all the peppery, herby character shoppers expect, while offering a lighter, high-protein alternative for easy everyday meals.”
The Cumberland Chicken Sausages join HECK!’s expanding chicken range, which includes sausages, burgers, seasoned mince and its innovative five-minute sausage rashers, made with no added nitrites.

items.body:
The John Lewis Partnership is to recruit more than 10,400 seasonal roles as it prepares for the ‘golden quarter’.
The vacancies span the breadth of Britain, reaching from Edinburgh to Exeter. Of the roles, 6,000 are within Waitrose’s 320 branches while 2,600 will be across John Lewis’ 36 shops. A further 1,800 will support across the retailer’s distribution centres and supply chain.
The Partnership will recruit from all ages and backgrounds, though the roles prove particularly popular amongst young candidates. Based on previous years’ numbers, around three quarters of the seasonal joiners were under 25.
With recent data showing one million young people in the UK are currently not in education, employment, or training (NEET), these positions offer a vital opportunity to gain valuable workplace skills and kickstart a career in retail, helping to address the increasing challenges this cohort faces in finding work.
Christmas remains by far the busiest period of the year for the Partnership and, whether customers are shopping in-store or online, this recruitment is focused on having Partners in the right places at the right times to make sure customer service remains consistently strong.
The hiring push follows significant investment – over £1bn at Waitrose and £800m at John Lewis – in both shops and in new technology designed to free up Partners’ time to focus on serving customers. As a result of the investment, Waitrose recently won the Grocer 33 Customer Service Award for the sixth consecutive year, and John Lewis was named Which? Retailer of the Year and the number one retailer in the UK Customer Satisfaction Index.
Helen Webb, Chief People Officer for the John Lewis Partnership, said: “These roles appeal to people of all ages and backgrounds, and we’re excited to welcome great candidates across the board. At the same time, we know retail is a vital stepping stone for young people entering the workforce. With youth unemployment remaining a significant challenge, we recognise the role we play in providing meaningful opportunities to learn and grow.
“Our seasonal roles are more than just a job for the festive period; for many, they are a catalyst for building confidence and kickstarting a long-term career. By offering thousands of roles to under-25s and guaranteeing interviews for care-experienced young people, we are actively helping to break down barriers to employment and investing in the future of our communities.”
Pay for the seasonal roles starts at £13.00 or £14.55 in London, rising to £13.25 and £14.80 after 30 days. Successful candidates will receive a competitive salary and training, as well as flexible and blended working options.
Guaranteed interviews for those with care backgrounds
As part of this broader commitment to young people, within the 10,400 roles the Partnership expects to recruit 100 young people who’ve experienced the care system, as part of its Building Happier Future programme. In June, it committed to recruiting a further 1,000 care-experienced young people by 2030. The move more than doubled its previous target, in recognition that the group faces some of the greatest barriers to finding work, through no fault of their own.
To support as many care-experienced young people as possible, it will also offer 300 welcome visits and 250 job-shadowing placements between now and December. Every young person who completes a job-shadowing placement will also be offered a guaranteed interview.
Golden quarter
Kicking off with the launch of new seasonal ranges, the build up to Black Friday in November, before moving into Christmas and John Lewis’ famous January Winter Sale, the so-called golden quarter is the retailer’s busiest period of the year.
Christmas comes early for retail; John Lewis sees a spike in online searches as the summer holidays end. In response to demand – particularly as customers look to spread the cost of Christmas – the John Lewis Christmas Shop launched online on 27 August, and is set to open in stores later this month. Waitrose’s Christmas range launches in shops from 21st September – with ‘The Food Lovers Christmas catalogue’ going live the same day, allowing customers to plan their menus and order early to beat the crowds.
Seasonal shop roles will go live at jlpjobs.com/Christmas this month, with candidates able to register their interest and sign-up for job alerts now.
Care-experienced people interested in the Building Happier Futures employability programme can contact buildinghappierfutures@

items.body:
Very, the online retailer operated by The Very Group, has launched its new multi-category Autumn campaign. The creative concept has been developed and led by its in-house brand team and internal creative agency, HelloStudio.
Across the campaign, which launched on Saturday (5th September), Very’s distinctive cube logo transports the viewer through a portal into a space filled with leading brands, flexible ways to pay, endless choice and unexpected discoveries, showcasing the best of the retailer’s Autumn offering. Fronting the campaign and hero TV advert is the 1999 Jamiroquai hit “Canned Heat.”
From getting back into weekday habits to planning ahead for busier days, the campaign taps into the familiar ‘reset’ that comes with the end of summer. Consumer mindset research shows that, for many, the switch from August to September marks the start of the Autumn Bustle, a shift in mindset centred around productivity and purpose*.
This moment, which sees the beginning of the new school year and families returning to more structured routines, presents an opportunity for Very to connect with customers and showcase everything it has to offer for the whole family across its multi-category department store.
With over 20 household names featured from across the online retailer’s department store offering – including Mango, ghd, Samsung, Nintendo, Nike and many more – the campaign showcases everything Very has to offer from brands and categories to the flexibility and convenience provided by the digital retailer.
Sam Wright, chief customer and commercial officer at The Very Group, commented: “This new campaign is all about bringing the full breadth of Very’s department store offer to life and giving customers more reasons to shop with us. For many people, there’s more to Very than they realise – whether that be range of products and brands, or the fact we offer compelling flexible payment options – we give customers convenience and flexibility, and that’s exactly what this campaign represents. This is the reason why we’ve introduced a new brand endline, ‘that’s the Very thing’, which speaks to the quality and versatility of our product offering.
“I’m also extremely proud because this new campaign has been produced almost entirely internally, with collaboration between our colleagues in marketing, retail, creative and production within HelloStudio.”
HelloStudio is The Very Group’s best-in-class internal creative agency, delivering high-volume ecommerce imagery alongside end-to-end, full-funnel campaigns across all categories. By combining bespoke content creation with cutting-edge technology—such as virtual production, AI-generated environments, and automated workflows for ecommerce and social media—HelloStudio pairs creative excellence with innovative efficiency to build deep consumer connections.
Julie Phelan, head of creative at HelloStudio, added: “This new campaign builds on our existing powerful brand codes and playful and accessible style. It’s a brilliant example of what we can achieve when we bring together talented people from across the business who understand our customers, our fantastic product offering and our ambitions for the future.”
The new campaign features a hero 30″ TV advert, along with an extensive suite of social-first content. The creative was developed by HelloStudio, with film production supported by Production Factory.
The campaign also includes a selection of bold and distinctive stills, and will run in the UK across TV, VOD, radio, social media, press and online. Media planning and buying was handled by Zenith.

items.body:
AO.com, the UK’s most trusted electrical retailer, has been announced as a principal partner of Manchester Fashion Week.
Alongside the runways, an AO exhibition will shine a light on how personal style extends beyond the wardrobe and into the home by encouraging customers to think differently about the products they live with and use every day, including making bolder decisions about the colour of appliances which can become expressions of individuality, as much as our clothes are.
Vicky Monk, AO’s retail director, said: “Fashion has always been about self-expression, but we believe that shouldn’t stop when you get home. The choices we make in our homes, like colour palettes and statement appliances, are another way of telling the world who we are.
“Products in our homes are some of the most-used and highest-value items, yet they’re rarely chosen with the same attention to personal style as clothing.
“We want to challenge that gap directly and show how these appliances can be the centrepiece of the room.”
Taking over a dedicated space in Versa Studios, AO will create an interactive space designed to explore how colour and personality can transform our spaces and the crossover between fashion and our homes.
The activation will present a range of colourful kitchen appliances in design-inspired spaces, encouraging visitors to think about their homes in the same way they curate their wardrobes. The installation will show how colour choices can reflect personal identity and help create spaces that feel uniquely individual.
It will also include a panel discussion, ‘Style Doesn’t Stop at Your Wardrobe’, with top experts in the home interiors and artistic spaces who will share their insights about incorporating colour and personality into your home. Speakers include interior designers Sophie Robinson and Matt Smith-Wood, alongside Manchester-based artist, Caroline Dowsett.
Monk added: “Not only are we celebrating local designers and artists through our sponsorship of Manchester Fashion Week, we’re also aiming to open customers’ eyes to the design possibilities offered by being braver with your appliance choices.”
The event and installation coincide with the upcoming colour edit launch on AO.com, with top products and guides on how to inject colour and style into your home.
Gemma Gratton, CEO of Manchester Fashion Week, said: “Fashion is expression, it’s how we communicate who we are, what we love, how we feel and how we want to be seen. But that expression doesn’t stop at what we wear. Our homes are an extension of that identity too; they reflect our personalities, our tastes, our moods and, ultimately, what makes us feel at home.
“At first, AO and Manchester Fashion Week might seem like an unusual pairing, but when you look at fashion through the lens of modern living, the connection is incredibly natural. The way we dress ourselves and the way we dress our spaces are both forms of self-expression.
“That’s exactly what Manchester Fashion Week is about – challenging perceptions, creating new conversations and looking at fashion through a much wider cultural lens. We’re delighted to have AO helping us explore that conversation this year.”
To find out more visit:  ao.com/manchester-fashion-week

items.body:
MINISO taps K-pop and Sephora takes next step on TikTok: last week’s biggest retail technology plays
RTIH rounds up the stand out retail systems deals, launches, deployments and pilots from the past seven days. Including JD Sports, HyperFinity, H&M Group, Alcampo, Hanshow, Instacart, World Market, Hungry Howie's, Asda, Vusion, MediaMarkt Saturn, Morrisons, The Home Depot, and Sainsbury's.
Morrisons
NIQ and Morrisons have announced a collaboration involving analytics, omnichannel intelligence, and decision-making tools. By leveraging NIQ’s Full View approach, the UK grocery retailer says it is aiming to build “a comprehensive understanding of market dynamics across supermarkets, online grocery, convenience and emerging retail channels, allowing teams to identify growth opportunities and act with clarity and confidence”.
The tie up includes automated reporting capabilities and self-service analytics intended to streamline workflows and support agility across the business.
“Retailers today need the ability to seamlessly turn insight into action,” says Russell Sylvester, NIQ Retail Vertical Lead UK & IRE. “By combining market measurement, consumer intelligence, omnichannel analytics, and advanced capabilities within a single ecosystem, we aim to support Morrisons in building a robust platform for future growth.”
Jen Price, Customer Director at Morrisons, says: “We’re excited to be launching this new collaboration with NIQ, which will deliver product and category intelligence across the full breadth of our retail channels, unlocking value through great insights and helping us make the right decisions quickly, to drive our future growth.”
MINISO
MINISO, a lifestyle brand with over 8,200 stores across 112 countries and regions, offering the likes of IP collectibles and blind boxes, has launched a pop-up tour with K-pop star Lisa, kicking off in Thailand on 1st September before travelling to Japan and China in September, Indonesia in October, and United States in November, with Mexico set to join at a later date.
Lalisa Manobal, aka Lisa, rose to prominence as a member of the South Korean girl group Blackpink, which debuted in 2016 and went on to become one of the best selling girl groups of all time.
Her collection with MINISO features more than 70 items across categories including bags, apparel, blind boxes and lifestyle accessories. It also includes the Yoyo × Lisa Collection Vinyl Plush Suprise Box series, featuring MINISO’s own artist IP, YOYO. In addition to a global product lineup, exclusive regional items and limited edition releases will be introduced.
The aforementioned tour kicked off with the opening of an official pop-up store at retail and lifestyle destination ICONSIAM in Bangkok from 1st-24th September. This includes immersive experiences and large scale visual takeovers across more than 250 screens throughout the mall, alongside four multi-story banners suspended in the central atrium.
Ecommpay
With a focus on one off payments such as tips and donations, Ecommpay has launched QR Code Payment, providing a single static QR code which merchants can display anywhere, whether on a printed sign, a receipt, or a web page. Payment amounts can be preselected or set by the consumer, and payment can be made using any available method.
The QR code is created, customised and published directly from the Ecommpay dashboard without development or integration work or coding required. It is also delivered on a fully merchant branded hosted payment page.
“We have built QR Code Payments to make it quick and simple to send one-off payments - the digital equivalent to leaving a £5 note tucked under a glass when you leave the table or throwing a few coins into a collection bucket as it passes,” comments Artus Zaremba, Head of Payment Solutions, Ecommpay. “Fewer customers carry cash today, so servers and charities can miss out even if someone wants to leave a tip or make a donation. With QR Code Payment, merchants and charities can display a static QR code to help capture these payments.”
Alcampo
Chinese firm Hanshow is working with Alcampo (Auchan Retail), a Spanish grocery retailer, on the roll-out of electronic shelf labels across 84 supermarkets.
With more than 560,000 ESLs being deployed, the initiative will help eliminate approximately 1,843 km of paper price strips annually, avoiding an estimated 8.4 tonnes of CO₂ emissions each year while supporting Alcampo's broader sustainability goals.
Beyond reducing paper consumption, ESLs provide a centralised platform for pricing and shelf-edge communication, helping ensure accurate and up-to-date product information across stores. The solution is also expected to reduce time spent on shelf-label updates and allow store teams to focus more on customer facing activities.
A spokesperson for Hanshow says: “We're delighted to partner with Alcampo as it continues to modernise store operations and advance a more sustainable retail environment.”
JD Sports
HyperFinity has partnered with JD Sports to design and deliver a personalisation programme that aims to equip the retailer with a clear evidence base for its loyalty strategy.
It has designed a personalisation engine and trialled this to build a framework for JD Sports UK. The solution was trialled to prove: The value of ‘buy again’ category offers to assess how active customers respond to identify the optimal spend multiplier incentives; The optimal incentive mix for high and low spenders for cash-based rewards versus spend multipliers; The ability to drive incremental basket spend through cross-sell offers aligned to previous purchase history, testing product affinity and which category follow-ons drive incremental spend.
According to those involved, the trials established that relevance consistently outperforms simply increasing incentive value, and that higher spenders respond better to spend multipliers, while lower spenders react similarly to both. Alongside this, they identified that campaign spacing must be tailored to individual behaviour to avoid offer fatigue.
The partnership delivered a significant material impact on topline performance, including an uplift in total in-store loyalty sales across JD Sports UK during the trial period. Based on the results, JD Sports has identified a multi-million pound opportunity to grow in-store loyalty sales within the first year of scaling the programme.
In addition to the analysis, HyperFinity delivered a suite of assets, including measurement dashboards, customer segmentations, campaign templates, and product seasonality and affinity insights, enabling JD Sports to continue building on the programme.
Minor Hotels
Checkout.com has announced a partnership with Minor Hotels, a hospitality group with more than 640 hotels across 67 countries. This involves it providing global acquiring and payment optimisation capabilities for Minor Hotels’ resort properties across multiple markets worldwide.
The partnership will also bring together Checkout.com’s Intelligent Acceptance and Dynamic 3DS Authentication capabilities. Intelligent Acceptance is the FinTech’s AI driven engine that enhances the performance of transactions and is powered by global network intelligence. It maximises first attempt approvals and reduces failed transactions. Dynamic application of 3DS authentication is based on issuer preferences and local regulatory requirements, reducing unnecessary friction for guests.
Anthony Green, Global Head of Digital Marketing and Ecommerce at Minor Hotels, says: “As our portfolio continues to grow across markets, we need payment infrastructure that is reliable, flexible and able to support a premium experience for our guests. Checkout.com’s global acquiring capabilities and payments expertise will help us simplify complexity, improve performance and build a stronger foundation for our next phase of growth.”
H&M Group
GreyOrange reports that more than 3,800 retail locations globally now run on its technology, with the likes of H&M Group using its inventory software gStore.
The AI powered platform, which includes merchandising software and connects with technologies such as RFID (radio frequency identification) readers and smart mirrors, has managed approximately 200 million retail inventory items across live deployments.
It uses sensor agnostic technology, including overhead or handheld RFID readers, to locate specific inventory items to within three to five feet. It connects with sales data to inform retailers which SKUs sell the fastest and which get abandoned in fitting rooms, where to place products to optimise sales, and when stock is running low. This real-time inventory “heat map” helps associates quickly replenish shelves and find items for customers.
“Many of the world’s largest retailers run their core operations on GreyOrange. Their scale, operational complexity, and willingness to co-develop the future of omnichannel technology rather than simply adopt it have helped us shape how our platform performs,” says Akash Gupta, Co-founder and CEO at GreyOrange. “We’ve reached this milestone of 3,800 stores live thanks to customers like H&M Group, whose deep partnership empowers us to keep building physical AI solutions that fit how busy retailers operate.”
Sephora
Sephora has announced its debut on TikTok Shop. Piloting in the United States from 19th September, its Drop Shop experience will feature exclusive monthly drops, showcasing curated products from some of Sephora's most popular partner brands. Each featured brand will have a dedicated moment to bring its products to life, tell its story and connect with new audiences.
Each drop will include teasers, interactive experiences, and creator led content, encouraging consumers to guess the brand in the spotlight. The experience will culminate in an official TikTok LIVE with a celebrity host, brand founders, and creators to unveil the featured products, answer audience questions, engage with viewers in real-time, and showcase products available for purchase on TikTok Shop during the LIVE.
“Beauty discovery has always been core to Sephora’s ethos, and the rise of social commerce and digital marketplaces have reinforced the need to evolve how we engage with our beauty lovers. We already have an incredibly active beauty community on TikTok, so we are excited to take the next step and pilot the Sephora Drop Shop on TikTok Shop. This platform gives us a new way to interact with our existing customers, while extending our reach to a highly immersed beauty audience. Importantly, the launch signifies a natural progression in how we continue to lead and innovate in beauty retail,” says Artemis Patrick, President and CEO at Sephora North America.
Products featured in each monthly drop will launch exclusively through Sephora's TikTok Shop, with select items later rolling out to Sephora.com, in selected Sephora stores or through other retail partners. During the exclusive launch window, customers will still be able to preview the products on the Sephora site ahead of their wider availability.
World Market
Instacart and World Market have announced a new partnership. Through the Instacart Marketplace, World Market's assortment will be available for same-day delivery in as fast as one hour with no markups. Instacart is the retailer’s first and exclusive online same-day delivery partner.
"World Market has built an incredibly loyal following of customers who love discovering something new every time they walk through the door, and we're thrilled to bring that same feeling of discovery directly to their homes for the first time with the speed and convenience of same-day delivery," says Ryan Hamburger, Chief Commercial Officer at Instacart. "As the only online marketplace offering a wide variety of World Market products for delivery in as fast as an hour, we're proud to help customers get the things they love - from internationally inspired foods and beverages to unique, imported home decor."
"Partnering with Instacart is an exciting new chapter for World Market and a natural extension of our commitment to making the World Market experience as accessible and convenient as possible for our customers," says Eric Hunter, Chief Executive Officer at World Market. "Our stores are filled with inspiring finds from around the globe, and now, customers can have that same curated assortment delivered to their doorstep the same day. We couldn't be more excited to bring this convenience to both longtime World Market customers and to connect with an entirely new set of customers who are discovering us for the first time."
Lindas Dekor
StrongPoint has signed an agreement to deliver an AutoStore system for Lindas Dekor, a Norwegian online store and family business specialising in simple, affordable home improvement products.
The automated solution developed by StrongPoint combines the warehouse system itself with software to provide the retailer with increased efficiency, improved scalability, and long-term performance in e-commerce logistics. The solution comprises a capacity of 6,000 bins, two VersaPorts, and six robots.
Hungry Howie’s
Cartwheel, an AI powered delivery platform for restaurants, reports that Hungry Howie’s Pizza is adopting its Hybrid Delivery technology across its stores. Following a pilot, it is progressing with a phased roll-out across its nearly 500-location system, with all locations targeted to be live by Q2 2027.
The partnership builds on a broader technology modernisation Hungry Howie's set in motion earlier this year, extending that work from digital ordering into how orders actually get to the door.
Hybrid Delivery gives franchisees a single view of in-house and third-party delivery, with fulfillment powered by DoorDash Drive. It prioritises in-house fleets based on configurable factors such as proximity to the store, order value and driver availability, then automatically routes to third-party drivers when demand peaks. Operators can see every driver in real-time from one place, while automated rules handle the manual work required to coordinate delivery capacity.
McCain
As Brits headed to parks to enjoy a sunny bank holiday Monday this week, McCain was on hand to provide picnickers with free portions of its Crispy French Fries product. These were delivered by a Hussel drone at Brockwell Park in London from 11am to 6pm.
All fries were prepared in a controlled food truck environment, with no barbecues, open flames, or outdoor frying used in the park.
Laura Koscik, a spokesperson for McCain, says: "Tasty, crispy chips at a picnic? What an upgrade! We launched The Fry Drop to make Brits’ bank holiday picnics even more enjoyable in a fun and unexpected way. With a little help from our drones, we’re taking air frying to new heights, showing that delicious fries can make any get together even better.”
TheCode
Luxury fashion marketplace Love the Sales has rebranded to TheCode and relaunched with more than 100,000 curated styles across menswear, womenswear and accessories. TheCode is an invite only marketplace, with partners selected according to product quality, positioning and their adjacency to the wider assortment.
The aim here is to create a coherent fashion destination rather than an indiscriminate marketplace built around volume alone. A membership proposition is on the cards, offering benefits including early access to selected events and collections.
For brands and retailers, the venture says it offers a data led environment for reaching relevant customers, generating incremental demand and managing selected inventory separately from owned, full price channels. This allows partners to keep their core customers focused on new-season collections while placing surplus inventory within a distinct and considered environment.
Proprietary AI technology is designed to optimise how and when products are surfaced, helping partners minimise markdowns and maximise financial returns. AI powered onboarding, automated stock management and intelligent marketing also make it easier for partners to sell through the platform with minimal ongoing management.
“A large assortment only becomes valuable when customers can navigate it effectively. Our proprietary AI technology helps us understand product relevance, recognise intent and create a more individual edit for every shopper,” says David Bishop, Co-founder and CTO at TheCode. “Technology allows us to manage complexity for both customers and partners. The aim is not simply to show customers more products, but to help them discover the right products, and to help our partners achieve the right commercial outcome.”
Asda
Asda has completed the roll-out of eSELs across its Asda Express petrol stations, Asda Express locations and Asda petrol station estate, with the deployment covering over 550 stores.
In a LinkedIn post, Anthony McCarron, Projects, Propostions & Comms Manager at Asda, said: "This is a massive achievement across so many internal and external stakeholders, so thank you - big shout to Daniel Pelissier for leading this project from start to finish on time and on budget."
"Our Vusion eSELs, installed by our delivery partner Renovotec, are delivering a real step change for customers and colleagues. Thank you to Elecomm, MADIC UK, and Evolve for the infrastructure support in achieving this huge milestone for our convenience stores."
Sainsbury's
Sainsbury's is rolling out radio frequency identification (RFID) technology across its TU clothing departments in approximately 400 stores, with the project set for completion by early September.
This follows a pilot earlier this year, which enabled the retailer to improve its stock level visibility, speed up replenishment and manage stock more efficiently.
“Really proud of my team and the role they’ve played in deploying this project across our stores. A huge amount of work, collaboration and energy behind the scenes to bring this to life,” says Gillian Ekin, Head of Transformation and Operational Development at Sainsbury’s.
RTIH has reached out to Sainsbury’s regarding specifics of the implementation, such as suppliers involved, and we will update this article when we receive a response.
The Home Depot
The Home Depot has announced the US wide roll-out of new in-store capabilities for Magic Apron, its Al powered shopping assistant. Customers can open it in the retailer’s mobile app or scan a QR code on in-store signage.
"Customers come to The Home Depot for expert guidance, and we know they want their shopping experience to be easy and efficient," says Jordan Broggi, EVP of Interconnected Retail. "Magic Apron takes the best of our digital expertise and brings it into the physical store, creating a more connected shopping experience that helps customers find products, get project guidance and make decisions faster. Our associates remain at the centre of the shopping experience, and Magic Apron gives customers another way to access guidance and support while they're in our stores."
This is the Holy Grail of omnichannel retail, according to Michael Guzzetta, Retail Innovation & Strategy Leader at Cookie Plug San Antonio, and a former H-E-B executive.
In a LinkedIn post, he said: “It's moments like these when an AI assistant stops being just another digital feature and starts making physical promises a reality. Customers can ask questions by text, voice, or image. Then, Magic Apron can provide project guidance, check local availability, and even point someone to a specific aisle and bay. The model is the visible part for the customer, but the harder job will be for the back end teams to keep several operating systems honest at the same time: Local inventory; Aisle and bay mapping; Product compatibility; Store specific knowledge; The handoff to an associate when the answer is incomplete or wrong.”
He added: “Anyone who has worked around store systems knows that “aisle 14, bay 6” isn’t just a helpful customer answer... It’s a promise built on receiving, stocking, planogram changes, shrink, inventory accuracy, and whatever happened on the floor ten minutes ago. Now zoom out to a nationwide scale and the important questions change."
"How quickly does local reality reach the assistant? How does an associate correct a bad answer? Who owns the recovery when the guidance is technically sound but the product isn’t actually there?”
Magic Apron is compelling because it connects advice to the physical store, Guzzetta argues. Its biggest test will be how often the store can keep the promise its digital friend just made.
Mediamarkt Saturn
Mediamarkt Saturn has opened its tenth Tech Village, with the latest one being located in Cologne, Germany. In a LinkedIn post, Guido Monferrini, EVP and Regional CEO, said: “In 2020, we opened the very first Tech Village in Milan. This week marked an exciting new milestone: Tech Village Cologne is officially open!”
He added: “As our 10th Tech Village in Europe, it is built on years of experience, learnings and continuous innovation. One of our greatest challenges was to refresh and redefine the concept, transforming it into a modern, inspiring environment that reflects our future vision and serves as the blueprint for future European Tech Villages.”
“At its core, it is all about experience: we want to offer everyone the opportunity to discover and engage with the most cutting-edge, immersive technology. By combining inspirational experiences with personal consultation and seamless service, we build what matters most: lasting trust with our customers.”
Key features: A redesigned in-house store concept with a tech driven layout, large format digital media surfaces, and an atmospheric lighting design; Immersive 3D experiences bringing products and technology to life alongside 31 brand boutiques; Integrated Xperion: Bringing a 1,000+ sqm gaming destination and 200-seat arena under the same roof.
Monferrini concluded: “Bringing a vision of this scale to life is a demanding and complex undertaking. The successful realisation of this project is the result of the dedication, expertise, creativity and teamwork demonstrated throughout every phase of the journey. A heartfelt thank you to my concept and construction team and to the German team for their fantastic collaboration on this remarkable achievement.”

Calum Johns joins fast food giant McDonald's UK as its Head of CRM, Loyalty, Partnerships And Social
McDonald's UK has appointed Calum Johns as Head of CRM, Loyalty, Partnerships & Social. He joins from Holland & Barrett, where he served as Head of Loyalty. Johns has also worked at Costa Coffee, Subway and InterContinental Hotels Group.
In a LinkedIn post, he said: "Four weeks into a dream role at a dream brand, and you could say: I’m lovin’ it. Thank you to all my amazing new colleagues and leaders for giving me the warmest of welcomes to the Arches. It’s already feeling like a very special place."
"Early wins: Joined the 5-a-side marketing team (current champions); Sampled a modest portion of the menu; Presented to our leadership team and franchisees; First team social locked and loaded; Very excited for what’s ahead with this team!"
New voice
Earlier this year, McDonald’s UK announced that English actor, producer, and screenwriter Stephen Graham had become the new voice of the brand, taking over from Dexter Fletcher.
According to a press release: “As one of the UK’s most recognisable and distinctive voices, Graham brings strong cultural resonance and everyday relatability. Graham’s selection will strengthen McDonald’s connection with younger audiences while maintaining broad, cross generational appeal in contemporary British culture.”
Graham’s appointment came as McDonald’s focuses on more insight led, culturally relevant storytelling rooted in real moments and fandom. His voice will feature across McDonald’s UK advertising. His first four voiceovers went live on 28th April and are for “McCrispy”, “Big Arch”, and “Breakfast Done Properly”, running across TV and radio.
Hannah Pain, Marketing & Menu Director, McDonald’s UK & Ireland, says: “Stephen brings a rare combination of cultural credibility and everyday warmth that feels perfectly aligned with where McDonald’s is today. As we continue to embrace a more culture first approach, his voice helps us connect with audiences in a way that feels honest, contemporary and familiar, building on the brilliant legacy Dexter created with us over many years.”

items.body:
The Range set to roll out VoCoVo Headsets across all 283 locations following one-store trial
VoCoVo has announced a partnership with home, leisure and garden retailer The Range, that will see Series 5 (S5) Pro Headsets and Call Points rolled out across all 283 of its stores. This follows a one-store trial over the course of a year.
The Range colleagues will get instant, hands free communication through the headsets, replacing disruptive loudspeaker calls and reducing the need for them to search the shop floor for one another. The technology will help deliver faster, more responsive customer service by reducing waiting times at tills, service desks and across the shop floor.
Colleagues can contact managers and team members immediately for price and stock checks, quickly coordinate requests and assign tasks in real-time, while two-way Call Points will allow customers to request assistance at the touch of a button and connect with available colleagues.
A Store Manager at The Range says: “The headsets have made a hugely positive impact in-store for both colleagues and customers. Customer service has noticeably improved as queries are answered faster, stock checks are smoother and warehouse to shop floor communication is instant. This has already streamlined Deliveroo and Click & Collect, and I can see the headsets becoming invaluable during patio season. They’ve become essential to daily operations."
“The very impressive results already achieved in our store have laid the groundwork for much bigger savings across the store network. I can’t wait to see colleagues benefitting from the same technology.”
Beth Worrall, CEO at VoCoVo, says: “The initial trial with The Range has shown how they can achieve significant time and cost savings while maintaining outstanding service levels and the optimum in-store experience at the same time. We’re looking forward to working alongside the team to implement the technology across all its stores.”
So hot right now
VoCoVo is included in RTIH’s first ever Retail Technology Hot 100 List. Launching in August, this sees us bringing you the hottest companies whose solutions and systems are helping drive the retail sector forward.
Our Founder and Editor, Scott Thompson, drew up a list of 150 companies that had consistently been on his radar over the past 12 months whilst bringing our community the latest retail tech news and views that matter. These companies operate across the omnichannel retail landscape (stores, online, mobile, supply chain, payments etc).
Our judging panel, including Vineta Bajaj, Group CFO, Holland & Barrett, Dan McGrath, JD Group Customer Operations, JD Sports, Dr. Astha Purohit, Director of Product Management, Customer Data and Identity, Walmart, and Paula Bobbett, Chief Data and Digital Officer, Boots, provided feedback on those who have the most innovative, forward thinking technology offerings and are also best addressing retailers' current challenges, painpoints, and opportunities.
The judges used the following framework when making their picks:
1. Retailer problem fit - how meaningful, strategic, and widely felt the retailer pain being addressed is.
2. Production traction in retail (2025–2026) - real named retailer deployments, pilots. 
3. Innovation and defensibility - genuine technical novelty paired with a defensible competitive position.
And there was also a public vote, with thousands of members of our community of retail tech enthusiasts getting involved. Thanks to all those who took part! Based on the judging panel's feedback and the public vote, we then drew up our first ever RTIH Retail Technology Hot 100.
So, without further ado, here are the 100 hottest global retail technology ventures right now. Drum roll, please…

items.body:
Midlands Air Ambulance Charity taps Minimist AI powered system to boost charity's online retail income
Midlands Air Ambulance Charity is using AI to improve how donated goods are processed for sale online, helping to generate additional income.
The technology is being introduced across the charity’s retail network, which includes shops in Hereford, Gloucester, Market Drayton, Merry Hill, Ross-on-Wye, Shrewsbury, Stoke-on-Trent, Tipton, Wellington, West Bromwich and Worcester.
Provided by Minimist, the new AI powered system enables shop teams to create online listings across platforms such as eBay and Vinted by taking a single photograph of a donated item. In under 30 seconds, it can generate a complete listing, including a product description, pricing suggestion, size information and virtual model imagery where appropriate, giving donated goods access to a wider audience while helping retail teams process stock more efficiently.
Midlands Air Ambulance Charity does not receive any government funding and relies entirely on public contributions to operate its lifesaving service. Every sale made through its shops and online marketplaces helps fund its helicopters, fleet of critical care cars as well as the specialist crews and equipment required to deliver pre-hospital emergency care across its six country region.
Amy Petherick, Regional Manager at Midlands Air Ambulance Charity, says: “Introducing Minimist is a major step forward for our retail operation. It allows our shop teams to process more donated items, create professional online listings quicker, easier and reach more buyers through online marketplaces. Most importantly, every additional sale helps generate vital income to keep delivering our lifesaving service. This technology has the potential to make a real difference to our fundraising and, ultimately, the communities we serve.”
Lauren Davies, UK Sales Executive at Minimist, says: “Minimist was developed specifically to support charity retailers with the challenges of processing and selling donated stock online. We are proud to support Midlands Air Ambulance Charity as it explores how AI can help its teams and volunteers work more efficiently.”

items.body:
Fynd founder Sreeraman Mohan Girija: here’s why agentic commerce represents the next frontier of retail
The part of retail no one is talking about is where agentic commerce pays off first, says Sreeraman Mohan Girija, Founder at Fynd.
Every conversation about AI in retail ends up in the same place: discovery. How does a customer find the right product? How does an agent suggest the perfect outfit, get the size right, and take someone from a vague idea to a completed purchase? It is a compelling picture. But it is not where most retailers should start.
The clearest, fastest commercial case for agentic commerce sits somewhere far less exciting. It sits in the moment after the order is placed.
Think about what happens when a parcel does not arrive. The customer opens an app, looks for a way to get in touch, waits in a queue, explains the problem to someone who pulls up the order, checks the tracking, and eventually offers a resolution. The whole thing takes time, costs money, and often leaves the customer more frustrated than the original issue did. Now multiply that across a peak trading week. The cost is not just operational. Every one of those interactions is a loyalty decision.
An AI agent handles this differently. It finds the customer, pulls up the order, sees that the delivery window has passed, and offers three options - refund, replacement, or reroute. The customer picks one. It is done. No queue. No ticket. No one manually updating three different systems. Two minutes, and the customer has a confirmation in their inbox.
This is not a concept. It is running in production today. And the business case for it is about as clear as it gets.
UK retailers lost £27 billion to online returns in non-food categories in 2024. Handling returns is expensive. The customer experience around post-purchase queries is consistently one of the weakest parts of the retail journey.
Nearly half of all returns come down to sizing, fit, or colour being different from what the customer expected. A further 14% are caused by product descriptions that simply were not accurate enough. These are not edge cases. They are recurring, predictable costs and they are concentrated exactly where an agent can step in.
There is another reason to start here, beyond the numbers. It comes down to trust.
Customers are more comfortable letting an agent sort out a problem they already have than letting one spend their money. The risk of a wrong answer in post-purchase is manageable. If the agent offers the wrong option, the customer picks a different one. If an agent places the wrong order on someone's behalf, that is a harder problem to fix. Beginning where the stakes are lower means you build confidence in the system before you ask more of it.
It also makes success easy to measure. In the early stages of any deployment, you need to know quickly whether it is working. Post-purchase gives you that. How many queries is the agent resolving without a human stepping in? How much faster is it than the old process? How many customers are getting what they need without calling? These numbers show up immediately, and they make the case for doing more far easier to build internally.
What separates a post-purchase agent that works from one that disappoints is the same thing that determines outcomes across all agentic commerce: what the agent is connected to. An agent that cannot see live inventory cannot confirm whether a replacement is available.
One that cannot access the order management system cannot process a refund. One without accurate delivery data cannot tell a customer where their parcel is. The conversation is the visible part. The systems underneath it are what make the answer right or wrong.
This is why getting the operational foundations in order matters so much. Every post-purchase query the agent handles well is a data point. Every customer who gets a fast, accurate answer is more likely to trust the agent next time, and more likely to let it do more. The move from post-purchase resolution to product recommendations to autonomous reordering is not a jump. It is a natural progression, and it starts here.
Some retailers are putting all their energy into building the most sophisticated product discovery experience possible. That will matter. But they are skipping past the part of the journey where the commercial return is most immediate, the trust requirement is lowest, and the learning builds fastest.
Start where the customer already needs help. Start where the costs are visible and the value is easy to measure. Start after the order, not before it. The front of the funnel gets all the attention. The back of it is where the money is.

items.body:
Simbe brings in former Meta, JPMorgan, American Express exec Claudia Molina as VP of Client Success
Physical AI and shelf intelligence specialist, Simbe, has announced the appointment of Claudia Molina as Vice President of Client Success, alongside new roles for Senior Vice President of Marketing Caitlin Allen and Senior Vice President of Strategy & Client Success Benjamin Bond at Food Marketing Institute (FMI).
Molina joins following roles at Meta, JPMorgan and American Express, where she led customer strategy, operational transformation and enterprise growth initiatives. At Simbe, she will guide executive customer relationships, long-term success strategies and transformation programmes.
"Physical AI offers an entirely new operating layer for retail," says Brad Bogolea, CEO and Co-Founder at Simbe. "The opportunity extends beyond identifying what's happening on a shelf. Trusted, real-time ground truth of the store enables retailers to orchestrate actions across channels. Claudia brings the strategic and enterprise experience to help our clients realise that value at scale."
Allen, meanwhile, has been appointed to FMI's Daunting Data Dilemma Industry Task Force, where she will contribute to industry efforts focused on retail data quality, interoperability and real-time operational visibility. Bond has joined FMI's Fresh Food Leadership Council, contributing expertise to initiatives focused on improving forecasting, reducing food waste and increasing visibility across fresh operations.
"We're pleased to welcome Caitlin Allen and Benjamin Bond to these important industry leadership roles, where their combination of retail expertise, technology leadership and operational perspective will strengthen the work of our committees," says Doug Baker, Vice President of Industry Relations at FMI. "We look forward to collaborating with them as FMI's Daunting Data Dilemma Industry Task Force and Fresh Food Leadership Council advance practical frameworks and best practices for the food retail industry."

Jay Thapar takes on influencer and creator partnerships role at high street comeback kid Bodycare
Jay Thapar has joined Bodycare as Head of Influencer & Creator Partnerships. In a LinkedIn post, Thapar, whose CV includes stints at The Beauty Crop and L'Oréal, said: "A beauty retailer where commerce meets culture and creators are at the centre of it. I’m excited to help shape what comes next, build partnerships that actually make an impact and create some serious noise along the way."
Comeback kid
Bodycare opened the doors to its third Studio Store at Highcross Leicester on Saturday 5th September. This built on launches in Sheffield and Derby.
Last year, Bodycare closed all its stores after collapsing into adminstration. Its brand and intellectual property were acquired out of administration in late 2025 by an investor group led by former The Body Shop and Molton Brown CEO Charles Denton, and it is now aiming to open 15 UK stores in 2026, growing to 150 locations over the next five years.
At the heart of the Leicester location will be a free to use Creator Studio, giving local creators, influencers, charities, schools, clubs and community groups a professional space to create, collaborate and share their stories.
Denton said: “The welcome we’ve received since bringing Bodycare back to the high street has been incredible, and we’re absolutely delighted to be bringing our next-generation Studio Store to Leicester. Leicester is a city with a huge sense of identity, community and creativity, exactly the qualities we want to build into our new stores.”
“The Creator Studio gives local people and organisations a place to create, connect and have their voices heard, while our customers can discover great value, new experiences and the brands they know and love.”

Interview: The tech stack helping ‘q-commerce’ scale at Tesco
Computer Weekly gets the lowdown on the tech stack supporting one of Tesco’s fastest-growing business areas from the man overseeing digital customer experience for grocery home shopping at the UK’s largest retailer
For many retailers, quick commerce (q-commerce) has been characterised by standalone technology stacks, dedicated fulfilment networks, and outsourced partnerships with third parties. The UK’s largest retailer, Tesco, has taken a markedly different route.
Rather than building a separate rapid delivery operation, the UK’s largest retailer has embedded its rapid delivery service, Whoosh, within its existing digital, fulfilment and store technology platforms. The result – five years from inception – is a proposition that is now accessible to more than 74% of the UK population and processes around 300,000 orders each week, while sharing core capabilities with Tesco’s wider online grocery operation.
Sales via Whoosh were up by 51% in the year to the end of February 2026, surpassing £400m.
Whoosh seemingly offers a case study in how enterprise retailers can scale new digital propositions without creating technical debt, duplicate platforms or organisational silos – three challenges often holding retailers back, as our recent interview with Ann Summers’ technology and supply chain director Jeannette Copeland underlined.
According to Kawaldeep Anand, head of product – digital customer experience (CX) for Whoosh and Tesco’s grocery home shopping division, the service’s success has been driven by building on Tesco’s existing technology estate rather than replacing it.
“Whoosh hasn’t been built as a separate proposition,” he says. “It has been built as part of our wider digital and store ecosystem.”
That philosophy has shaped every stage of the platform’s evolution over the past five years.
Platform thinking
As demand for rapid grocery delivery has accelerated, particularly during the coronavirus pandemic when partnerships such as Boots and Deliveroo and Asda and Uber Eats were established to cater to the unprecedented consumer need for q-commerce, Tesco resisted creating a standalone application, fulfilment platform or engineering organisation.
Instead, the retailer integrated Whoosh into the same customer-facing digital channels, core retail services and operational platforms already supporting its wider grocery business.
  Kawaldeep Anand, Tesco 
“This has allowed us to grow the service in a measured way using our existing store network, our familiar app and website, our Clubcard capabilities, our fulfilment technology and our delivery partner network,” Anand explains.
From a technology perspective, this has apparently created several advantages. Existing services could be reused, engineering investment benefited multiple business units simultaneously, and innovations developed for Whoosh could flow back into Tesco’s broader retail platform.
“It has given us a chance to test and refine the technology, improve the operating model, and to listen to colleagues and customer feedback along the way,” says Anand. “As a result, we’ve built a robust, resilient, scalable technology solution that benefits the whole Tesco Group rather than just a rapid delivery platform.”
A tech stack built largely in-house
At the centre of Whoosh sits a technology platform that Tesco has overwhelmingly developed internally.
“Almost the entire technology stack behind Whoosh, from customer-facing applications through to the APIs [application programming interfaces] that power the service, is bespoke and designed, built and managed by the Tesco Technology division,” says Anand.
The architecture comprises four primary layers. The CX layer delivers Whoosh through the existing Tesco mobile app and Tesco.com, allowing customers to use familiar payment methods, Clubcard functionality and digital journeys rather than switching to a separate rapid-commerce application.
Supporting this is the colleague and fulfilment layer, which connects store-based picking applications with Tesco’s retail and fulfilment platform. These services orchestrate inventory availability, pricing, payments, customer orders, routing, capacity planning, picking workflows and marshalling.
The third layer integrates external delivery providers, including Uber Eats, Just Eat and Stuart, through APIs that manage dispatch, collection, delivery tracking and customer notifications. As order volumes have increased, Tesco has continually evolved these integrations to improve resilience and operational scalability, according to Anand.
Completing the architecture is a data and analytics layer that provides operational visibility across customer demand, fulfilment efficiency and platform performance, allowing product and engineering teams to optimise capacity, improve CX, and identify opportunities for continuous improvement.
Third-party technology is used selectively where it provides clear value. For example, Tesco continues to use Worldpay as its payments gateway. However, Anand stresses that the core CX, fulfilment logic, orchestration services and Clubcard integration remain proprietary capabilities developed by Tesco Technology.
For Tesco, that level of ownership delivers an important strategic advantage – the ability to evolve rapidly without depending on supplier roadmaps or undertaking major platform replacements.
Stores for scale
Building the platform was only one challenge. Scaling it across hundreds of stores presented another.
Unlike rapid-commerce specialists built around dark stores, Tesco needed to enable physical stores to support traditional retail operations while simultaneously functioning as local fulfilment hubs.
“The store network is central to the model,” says Anand. “Stores are close to customers, they already hold the grocery inventory, and they are already part of their local communities.”
The engineering challenge therefore became one of orchestration rather than infrastructure.
“The technology challenge is to make that network even more responsive to their communities, so a store can serve customers shopping in person and ordering digitally.”
When Whoosh expanded into Tesco Express stores, the operational model became significantly more complex. Smaller footprints, reduced staffing levels and different workflows meant existing systems required adaptation rather than simple replication. Tesco responded by redesigning order-picking applications, colleague messaging and fulfilment workflows specifically for convenience stores.
The retailer also developed new catchment optimisation algorithms that balance customer demand, picking capacity and delivery partner availability to maximise fulfilment performance while protecting delivery promises.
Notably, these enhancements were introduced without deploying additional physical tech devices into stores, reducing implementation complexity and minimising operational disruption, according to Anand.
“If you needed evidence that rapid delivery can be successfully integrated into a wider retail operating model rather than treated as something separate from stores, we’re it,” he says.
Cross-functional product engineering
Whoosh’s organisational model mirrors its platform architecture.
What began as a small innovation team has evolved into multiple multidisciplinary squads spanning product management, engineering, programme delivery, user experience, experimentation, analytics and data science.
“The early 0-to-1 journey was driven by close collaboration between our business and Tesco Technology teams,” Anand explains.
  Kawaldeep Anand, Tesco 
Today, those teams own products throughout their lifecycle, enabling rapid experimentation alongside operational accountability.
“Our way of working is important. Whoosh is a live service operating at pace and scale, so these multidisciplinary teams own products and services end-to-end. They need to be able to experiment, iterate quickly, and work closely with store operations and business teams to solve practical challenges.”
Crucially, according to Anand, Tesco avoided creating isolated engineering capabilities for rapid commerce.
“We deliberately avoided creating a standalone technology stack for rapid delivery to make sure innovation flowed through the business both ways – from the wider business to Whoosh and vice versa,” he says.
AI accelerating product delivery
Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly supporting both software delivery and operational optimisation across Tesco Technology.
“Our approach is practical, and we see it as a powerful tool as opposed to a standalone capability,” says Anand.
Within Whoosh, AI is already being applied throughout the product development lifecycle, supporting rapid prototyping, design analysis, insight generation, experimentation and testing.
“This helps our teams move from idea to evidence more quickly,” he adds.
Operationally, Tesco has already demonstrated measurable benefits. AI-enabled scheduling tools created an additional 100,000 online delivery slots in the week before Christmas, while Whoosh attracted more than 250,000 new customers in the same period, according to Anand.
Looking ahead, Tesco sees opportunities in AI-enabled product discovery, conversational commerce and shopping journeys delivered through messaging platforms including WhatsApp.
“The important point is that customers and colleagues may not always see AI directly,” says Anand. “Instead, they experience the benefits through services that feel more relevant, more reliable and easier to use.”
Business performance metrics
Tesco acknowledges the pace of rapid commerce demands a product operating model built around continuous delivery rather than periodic releases.
According to Anand, product managers spend their time balancing customer needs, engineering priorities and operational realities through constant collaboration with business, engineering, user research, data science and operations teams.
Ideas are validated through experimentation and A/B testing before broader deployment, ensuring product decisions remain evidence-based.
“The work is both practical and strategic, and success is measured by business performance metrics, not outputs,” he says.
  Kawaldeep Anand, Tesco 
As Whoosh enters its next phase of growth, Tesco’s priorities remain closely aligned with its platform strategy.
Expansion will focus on extending geographical coverage, increasing store participation, broadening the available product range and continuing to personalise the CX through data-driven capabilities. There is also a recognition within Tesco that rapid delivery itself is evolving.
“Rapid delivery started with emergency top-ups,” says Anand. “That’s still important, but customers are increasingly using Whoosh for broader baskets.”
The retailer is already experimenting with larger basket sizes and later same-day fulfilment in selected locations, creating new use cases that bridge traditional grocery delivery and immediate convenience shopping.
From a technology perspective, that evolution looks set to rely on the same architectural principles that have underpinned Whoosh since its 2021 launch.
“We will continue to make the experience more personalised and intuitive by making it easier to build baskets, improving access to Clubcard rewards and using data and customer insight responsibly to create a more relevant shopping experience,” Anand notes.
Tesco’s strategy demonstrates that rapid commerce, q-commerce, or speedy delivery – whatever a retailer refers to it as – does not necessarily require separate technology estates or independent operating models. Instead, by treating it as another capability within a common platform, Tesco has created an architecture supporting both innovation and long-term scalability – a crucial combination in a retail world that never stands still.
