items.title: HFSS promo ban poses the question, will advertising help c-stores? Viewpoint: James Dunaj
items.summary: For those impacted, volume discounts and prime positioning for HFSS are over. The question remains, could brands use advertising to drive more footfall and sales? There have been many issues for convenience stores to mull over with the introduction of HFSS restrictions. There were initial… This story continues at HFSS promo ban poses the question, will advertising help c-stores? Viewpoint: James Dunaj Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
There have been many issues for convenience stores to mull over with the introduction of HFSS restrictions. There were initial questions over whether a store is affected and, if so, where should HFSS products go? The overarching unknown, though, remains what comes next for store managers wanting to grow sales?
The end of September and start of October are the final deadlines for HFSS in England and Scotland respectively. Although the new regulations are already in place in England, the end of the month marks the final day volume-based promotions printed on old stock can still be displayed. In Scotland, it’s the full introduction of the new regulation. Transition periods are over, for impacted stores it really is the end of volume-based discounting and prime positioning.
These in-store promotions and placements have been proven to drive up sales and profitability, particularly when a price cut has been funded by the manufacturer. With an end to such deals and no more prime placements for impacted stores, owners are naturally curious about other way to drive up basket sizes. The Government insists stores are not set to lose money through the new regulations and that spending will shift to more healthy options that could perhaps see sales revenue increase.
Can advertising help?
Manufacturers are asking the same questions and have been looking at a very old question in convenience and impulse purchases. In the absence of “3 for 2” and end of aisle positioning, could advertising lift sales?
It’s a question that has yet to be answered scientifically because it’s been very difficult to say for sure one way or the other. As any convenience store manager will know, confectionery and snacks are often impulse purchases. If a person didn’t enter a store intending to buy a specific product, how would anyone know if an advert prompted them to put a snack in their basket or whether it was just an unconscious impulse to treat themselves?
We thought we’d provide food manufacturers and retailers with an answer. Circana’s in a fortunate position of being able to track sales down to single product level across much of the UK. Working with one of our close media partners, we were able to build out a measurement test to compare the direct impact of campaigns on sales.
We didn’t want to just see if advertising worked, we wanted to show how each channel impacts revenues. This is more crucial now than previously due to the new rules banning HFSS product advertising online as well as on television before 9pm. Brand advertising is permitted, so long as HFSS products do not feature. Outdoor and radio are not affected, although there is still a ban if more than a quarter of an audience are under 16 or the site is within 100 metres of a school. It should be added that some councils have barred HFSS ads on their outdoor screens, as has TfL.
To get a definitive answer for a well-known confectionery brand, we built out four different test cells containing a similar number of stores where sales levels were comparable. We had individual test cells for outdoor, online and radio advertising as well as an omnichannel area where all three forms of advertising ran together. We also included a control cell which had no advertising present, so we had a comparison area to understand the advertising’s true impact.
Good news with a halo
The results showed that advertising increases revenue, in different ways for each channel. Outdoor has an early lift in sales which online maintains for the entire campaign period. Radio stood out for giving an improvement at the end of the campaign and, interestingly, for a fortnight after. The best results, though, came from omnichannel advertising approach (all three channels combined) which saw a 3.5% sales rise and an ROI of £1.25 for every £1 put in. This confirms a well-known advertising belief that an ad campaign works best when multiple channels are used.
So, the answer was clear that advertising works for the brand’s campaign budget as well as a store’s cash register. It has to be said, of course, this was only for one campaign. For advertising, it proves hybrid campaigns work, where brand and product advertising work alongside one another on a combination of channels.
The part that may well interest store managers, as well as food companies, is that only does advertising work, it also improves sales across an entire range. We picked up a 2% rise in sales among products which didn’t feature in adverts. It may sound odd, but it’s the well-known halo effect. A person might be influenced to buy a product but not like the product variant in an advert and so they choose their preferred option, whether it was advertised or not.
For store managers learning to work with the new regulations this may come as a welcome piece of news.
While affected stores cannot run in-store volume promotions or put tempting snacks alongside the till queue, there is still the option for food and drinks brands to drive up revenue through compliant advertising that increases sales across a range, even for variants not included in the campaign.
James Dunaj is partner success director, Circana

items.title: Government must use budget to cut business costs if it wants growth, says ACS
items.summary: The Association of Convenience Stores (ACS) has called on chancellor John Healey to cut business rates, crime and the cost of employing people to help stores out of the “cost-of-trading crisis”. The ACS argues that in two years business rates bills have risen by more… This story continues at Government must use budget to cut business costs if it wants growth, says ACS Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
The ACS argues that in two years business rates bills have risen by more than 70%, while employer national insurance costs have almost doubled.
The national living wage has also gone up, with costly changes to employment rights, alongside volatile energy costs.
Local shops, says the ACS, “are being left with very little room to breathe”.
In the forthcoming budget, the ACS wants the small business rate relief multiplier reduced by the full 20p available to the government, and wants it to increase the point at which businesses start paying business rates to £18,000 rateable value.
On crime, the ACS would like money generated from the vaping products levy (‘vape tax’) to be used to enforce the law against those that sell illicit products and don’t follow rules.
ACS chief executive Ed Woodall said: “Convenience retailers across the country are struggling to make ends meet in the face of enormous financial pressures from business rates hikes, lost trade to criminals and illicit sellers, and the ever-rising cost of employing people.
“If the chancellor is serious about backing British businesses and creating good growth in every postcode, he must acknowledge the challenges facing local shops and take swift action.”

items.title: The Works secures heavyweight backing in activist investor row
items.summary: The Works has secured the backing of a pair of heavyweight shareholder proxies in the discount retailer’s boardroom tussle with an influential activist investor.  The stationary and crafts retailer has been locked in a row with Kelso, a London-listed investment firm, since the investor sought to force a director onto its board.  Institutional Shareholder Services [...]
items.body:
The Works secures heavyweight backing in activist investor row
The Works has secured the backing of a pair of heavyweight shareholder proxies in the discount retailer’s boardroom tussle with an influential activist investor.
The stationary and crafts retailer has been locked in a row with Kelso, a London-listed investment firm, since the investor sought to force a director onto its board.
Institutional Shareholder Services (ISS) and Glass Lewis, two top shareholder advisories, have urged investors in The Works to slap down Kelso’s proposal in a major boost to the retailer.
Kelso has claimed that Graeme Coulthard, a former Card Factor director and major shareholder in The Works, should join the board of the retailer.
But executives at The Works have claimed Coulthard’s presence on the board would “risk derailing” its growth strategy and refused to meet with the prospective director.
Ahead of the vote on Kelso’s proposal at next week’s Annual General Meeting (AGM), ISS told shareholders that the investment firm has “failed to articulate a compelling case for board change”.
Kelso has “not raised any material concerns regarding the company’s performance or strategy,” the proxy said.
Glass Lewis, another leading shareholder advisory, said the investor’s concern over The Work’s low share price “appears to have some merit”.
“[But] the case for electing [Coulthard] remains insufficient, particularly given the company’s improving operating performance and substantial recent shareholder returns.”
Kelso ‘perplexed’ by boardroom tussle
Last month, the boardroom spat took a turn when Kelso hit out at The Works chairman Stephen Bellamy for dialling in to board meetings from his home in New Zealand.
The activist investor said it “believes shareholders would benefit from greater clarity regarding [Bellamy’s] physical attendance and in-person engagement with the business.”
But Glass Lewis pointed to evidence that Bellamy attended all of the company’s seven boardroom meetings last year.
“In the absence of evidence that any presumed virtual participation has prevented Mr. Bellamy from effectively performing his duties as a director, this concern does not provide a sufficient basis for supporting the election of Mr. Coulthard,” the proxy said.
The Works has urged shareholders to vote down Kelso’s proposal, which it says would “create an imbalance in governance and potentially result in particular shareholder interests being prioritised over those of the broader shareholder base, with a consequent risk of value destruction.”
Kelso told its investors on Wednesday that it is “perplexed and disappointed that the current board have chosen to advise shareholders to reject [Coulthard’s] appointment.”
The investment firm is The Works’s third-biggest shareholder, owning 10 per cent of the company, while Coulthard has an eight per cent stake.
In recent years, The Works has sought to overturn its reputation as a ‘pile it high, sell it cheap’ retailer by pivoting to screen-free entertainment for children.
The retailer posted 3.3 per cent sales growth and £260m in revenue to May, pushing adjusted profit up 44 per cent to £7.2m.

items.title: ASDA’s progress remains fragile as its turnaround strategy stays under strain, says GlobalData

Following yesterday’s release of ASDA’s figures for the quarter ending 30 June 2026; Eleanor Simpson-Gould, Senior Retail Analyst at GlobalData, a leading intelligence and productivity platform, offers her view: “ASDA’s Q2 results reaffirm the grocer’s tenuous position in the UK food & grocery sector with sales continuing to fall. Total revenue excluding fuel decreased to […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Following yesterday’s release of ASDA’s figures for the quarter ending 30 June 2026; Eleanor Simpson-Gould, Senior Retail Analyst at GlobalData, a leading intelligence and productivity platform, offers her view: “ASDA’s Q2 results reaffirm the grocer’s tenuous position in the UK food & grocery sector with sales continuing to fall. Total revenue excluding fuel decreased to £5.1bn in the second quarter on an Easter-adjusted basis, down 3.9% on last year’s £5.3bn. The pace of decline has worsened through the first half of the year, with like-for-like (l-f-l) sales falling 2.3% in Q2, a steeper decline than the -0.8% reported in Q1. This is despite 18 months of work under the Formula for Growth plan. ASDA’s Q2 performance underlines how much ground it has to make up before its focus on price, range and availability translates into a genuine recovery in sales. ASDA must keep closing the gap on range and service in Q3 by ensuring its fresh and frozen range investment is felt consistently across stores, while ensuring its price investments stay front of mind for consumers.
“ASDA has invested in a stronger customer offer during Q2, including upgraded fresh and frozen ranges, over 400 new products and an extension of its Rewards loyalty scheme to Express stores. Yet, food l-f-l sales still fell 1.9% between April and June, providing little evidence that this investment has resonated with consumers. One encouraging development is the rollout of shelf-edge cameras, new technology designed to flag empty shelves so staff can restock before sales are lost. This investment is a positive signal that ASDA is targeting availability, which has weighed on its turnaround. However, the impact will only be proven once the cameras are rolled out more widely across stores.
“While ASDA’s outlook remains challenging, its seven-week trading statement to 18 August 2026, reporting a 0.2% uplift in ex-fuel l-f-l sales — its first growth in more than two years – appears to be an encouraging signal after a prolonged period of decline. However, the grocer’s food l-f-l sales rose 0.7% for the seven weeks, a weak return that also indicates a considerable lag in its non-food proposition. Furthermore, the period covered the World Cup and a run of heatwaves, both of which broadly lifted UK grocery spending, so some of this improvement will be a result of favourable conditions, rather than ASDA-specific gains alone. ASDA provided a similarly positive initial outlook for Q1, but that quarter ultimately ended with total revenue, excluding fuel, down 1.5%. A promising in-quarter trajectory has not yet translated into a positive result. ASDA needs to demonstrate that these early Q3 improvements can last throughout the entire quarter. Continued investment in keeping prices low compared to competitors is essential to avoid another temporary surge in what has been a prolonged decline.”

items.title: Poundland owners rush to sell discount retailer before Christmas
items.summary: The owners of Poundland are racing to find a buyer for the discount retailer ahead of the all-important Christmas trading period, having already received interest from suitors.  Gordon Brothers, who bought Poundland only a year ago, have appointed advisors Alvarez & Marsal (A&M) to sound out interest in the company after several parties approached the [...]
items.body:
Poundland owners rush to sell discount retailer before Christmas
The owners of Poundland are racing to find a buyer for the discount retailer ahead of the all-important Christmas trading period, having already received interest from suitors.
Gordon Brothers, who bought Poundland only a year ago, have appointed advisors Alvarez & Marsal (A&M) to sound out interest in the company after several parties approached the Boston-based investment firm about a potential takeover.
A&M have been told to hand Gordon Brothers a list of formal bids by the start of October, as the crucial Christmas trading period kicks off, City AM understands.
The advisors will be approaching financial investors and leading retailers to sound out their interest in a potential takeover in the coming weeks.
This rush process has been designed to secure Poundland’s future as soon as possible, with the hopes of minimising distraction from the busiest trading period of the year.
Gordon Brothers expects that Poundland’s sale will attract significant interest from across the retail sector, it is understood. Sky News first reported the timelines of the deal.
Poundland faced ‘difficult conditions’
The discount retailer has faced a difficult period in recent years, which its current owners have blamed on a challenging economic environment and a drastic restructuring.
The firm fell to an £85m pre-tax loss in the year to September, nearly doubling its £45m shortfall in the prior year. The group’s sales slipped 12 per cent to £1.5bn.
Poundland slashed its headcount by 11 per cent to 14,417 and closed nearly 200 stores in that year.
The company’s directors blamed its widening loss on “difficult trading conditions” and a “significant programme of restructuring”.
The retailer used 2025 as a “reset moment,” it said. “This led to a challenging set of numbers seen in these statutory accounts, but it has positioned the company as well as it could be in terms of its turnaround.”
But Gordon Brothers say Poundland has turned a corner since it bought the retailer for just £1 in July last year.
The group recently opened its first new store in two years and has been working to return its iconic £1 price point across its grocery range.
Barry Williams, managing director of Poundland, said: “Rebuilding trust with customers takes time, but we’re making very significant progress as we deliver the ranges and price simplicity they demand of us.”

items.body:
Icy. Cold. Intense. Stormy. For generations, women have been described using the language of the weather. Not always as a compliment.
In fact, there was a time when storms were named exclusively after women. Why? They were seen as wild, unpredictable and capable of leaving a lasting impact wherever they went.
It was meant as an insult, but this autumn, Sweaty Betty is reclaiming the forecast. Its new campaign Born for the Storm celebrates women who don’t wait for clear skies before getting on with it. The women who keep moving when life gets messy. The women who refuse to let a little turbulence get in the way and who never dial themselves down.
Rolling out across film, print, digital, retail, social, CRM, OOH and PR, Born for the Storm celebrates what it means to be a force of nature. And naturally, the outerwear built to weather it all.
The campaign heroes Nimbus, Sweaty Betty’s signature puffer and true design icon, which now holds UK Design Registration 6497980. Built for days when the forecast looks questionable, but our plans don’t, Nimbus treats bad weather exactly how it should be treated: as somebody else’s problem.
Alongside Nimbus sits Motion, the waterproof parka for women who aren’t waiting for perfect conditions. Lightweight, waterproof and designed to keep up, it’s proof that a little rain isn’t a very convincing excuse.
Both are designed to keep women moving. Full stop.
Melissa Mullen, Brand President, Sweaty Betty, says: “People have spent a long time comparing women to storms. We see it as a compliment and Born for the Storm celebrates that spirit. It’s about showing up, getting on with it and refusing to be held back by a little turbulence, whether that’s in the forecast or in life.”
Since 1998, Sweaty Betty has championed one belief: women shouldn’t have to shrink, soften or slow down. Its mission is simple: empower women through movement and give them the confidence to take on whatever comes next.
Born for the Storm launches on 2 September 2026. Sweaty Betty’s Autumn/Winter outerwear collection is available online and in store now.

items.body:
Aptos report: retailers heavily underestimating financial value of modernising their PoS systems
Aptos has released a new study conducted by Coresight Research. A key takeaway: 85% of retailers that have recently modernised their Point of Sale systems say the investment either met or exceeded their return on investment expectations. The report is based on a survey of 150 global retail decision-makers involved in PoS strategy, selection and modernisation.
“Modern PoS platforms, typically characterised by cloud native deployments, microservices-based architectures, mobile first development and API driven integration, help retailers adapt to the changing role of stores as well as shifts in consumer expectations,” the report states. “Retailers that view PoS modernisation as simply a checkout upgrade risk undervaluing its strategic and financial impact.”
Beyond the headline ROI finding, the study found that retailers that have modernised their PoS systems reported:
- A 1.2 percentage point average increase in in-store conversion rates.
- A 4.3% increase in average transaction value.
- 68% of retailers running cloud native PoS reported a moderate to high positive impact across operational efficiency, inventory visibility, customer experience and sales performance.
Additionally, Coresight Research modelled the impact of PoS modernisation for a hypothetical retailer with $1 billion in annual revenue and 750 stores, estimating $4.4 million in annual cost savings and $39.6 million in annual revenue uplift. The savings were based on reductions in costs associated with hardware, software, maintenance and IT support, with the revenue gains achieved through increased ATV, in-store conversions, network uptime and omnichannel orders.
At the same time, however, the report finds that many retailers have yet to complete the shift to modern, cloud native architecture. Currently, 22% of retailers operate hybrid or fully on-premises PoS environments, while 36% use cloud hosted systems that stop short of the flexibility, modularity and continuous update capabilities that cloud native platforms provide. Core PoS systems in use today have been implemented on average for 4.3 years, with 30% of respondents operating systems that are at least five years old.
The study also found that retailers that have already modernised consistently report stronger outcomes than expected by those still planning to invest. The largest gaps between realised benefits and objectives are in improvements in store productivity - 49% of modernisers achieved this outcome versus 24% of planners expecting it; mobile checkout enablement - 44% versus 20%; improvements in store conversion rates - 44% versus 27%; and improved real-time inventory visibility - 50% versus 36%.
The survey data shows that execution - not conviction - is what stands between retailers and realising that value. Integration complexity emerged as the most widely cited obstacle, with 45% of retailers that have modernised their PoS systems ranking it among their top three implementation challenges. Notably, difficulty justifying ROI to senior leadership emerged the least challenging, cited by just 19% of respondents.
“Retailers have moved past debating whether PoS modernisation pays off. The data and real-world results settle that question,” says Deborah Weinswig, CEO and Founder at Coresight Research. “As the conversation shifts from ‘why’ to ‘how,’ we see leading retailers investing in cloud native PoS platforms that are built from the ground up to streamline integration and partnering with vendors that can support their PoS transformation end to end.”
“This report confirms what we hear directly from our retail customers: the ROI is there and the path to capturing it is clearer than ever,” says David Bruno, Director of Retail Industry Insights at Aptos. “PoS modernisation can directly and positively impact nearly every aspect of retail operations. The key to capitalising on the opportunity is to select the right vendor who can guide you through the process and help you capitalise on the financial and operational benefits of modernisation while minimising disruption.”
So hot right now
Aptos is included in RTIH’s first ever Retail Technology Hot 100 List. Launching in August, this sees us bringing you the hottest companies whose solutions and systems are helping drive the retail sector forward.
Our Founder and Editor, Scott Thompson, drew up a list of 150 companies that had consistently been on his radar over the past 12 months whilst bringing our community the latest retail tech news and views that matter. These companies operate across the omnichannel retail landscape (stores, online, mobile, supply chain, payments etc).
Our judging panel, including Vineta Bajaj, Group CFO, Holland & Barrett, Dan McGrath, JD Group Customer Operations, JD Sports, Dr. Astha Purohit, Director of Product Management, Customer Data and Identity, Walmart, and Paula Bobbett, Chief Data and Digital Officer, Boots, provided feedback on those who have the most innovative, forward thinking technology offerings and are also best addressing retailers' current challenges, painpoints, and opportunities.
The judges used the following framework when making their picks:
1. Retailer problem fit - how meaningful, strategic, and widely felt the retailer pain being addressed is.
2. Production traction in retail (2025–2026) - real named retailer deployments, pilots. 
3. Innovation and defensibility - genuine technical novelty paired with a defensible competitive position.
And there was also a public vote, with thousands of members of our community of retail tech enthusiasts getting involved. Thanks to all those who took part! Based on the judging panel's feedback and the public vote, we then drew up our first ever RTIH Retail Technology Hot 100.
So, without further ado, here are the 100 hottest global retail technology ventures right now. Drum roll, please…
You can download the hot 100 in pdf format here, or flick through it here 👇👇👇 Enjoy!

items.body:
Emma Griffin departs John Lewis & partners for new challenge at RTIH Hot 100 List star FoundIt!
Emma Griffin has taken on the role of Customer Success Lead at FoundIt!. She joins from John Lewis & Partners where she spent 16 years, most recently serving as Product Manager.
In a LinkedIn post, she said: “After 16 amazing years with the John Lewis Partnership, moving into the world of intent led e-commerce and AI was always going to feel like a leap. What I didn't expect was how quickly it would start to feel like home.”
She added: “And what a start it's been! In my first week, FoundIt! was voted number ten in the RTIH Retail Technology Hot 100 by our peers in the industry, which means so much.
I've spent my whole career on the retailer side, so I know exactly how it feels when customers can't find what they came for. Getting to help fix that for Marks and Spencer, B&Q, Tradepoint, John Lewis & Partners, Neiman Marcus, and Michael Kors, and doing it without asking any of them to rip out what they already have, is a real privilege.”
Griffin concluded: “Thank you to the whole FoundIt! team for the warmest of welcomes, and to Retail Technology Innovation Hub for the recognition. Two weeks in, and I already know this was the right move. Here's to the next chapter.”
So hot right now
RTIH’s first ever Retail Technology Hot 100 List launched in August. We’re bringing you the hottest companies whose solutions and systems are helping drive the retail sector forward.
Our Founder and Editor, Scott Thompson, drew up a list of 150 companies that had consistently been on his radar over the past 12 months whilst bringing our community the latest retail tech news and views that matter. These companies operate across the omnichannel retail landscape (stores, online, mobile, supply chain, payments etc).
Our judging panel, including Vineta Bajaj, Group CFO, Holland & Barrett, Dan McGrath, JD Group Customer Operations, JD Sports, Dr. Astha Purohit, Director of Product Management, Customer Data and Identity, Walmart, and Paula Bobbett, Chief Data and Digital Officer, Boots, provided feedback on those who have the most innovative, forward thinking technology offerings and are also best addressing retailers' current challenges, painpoints, and opportunities.
The judges used the following framework when making their picks:
1. Retailer problem fit - how meaningful, strategic, and widely felt the retailer pain being addressed is.
2. Production traction in retail (2025–2026) - real named retailer deployments, pilots. 
3. Innovation and defensibility - genuine technical novelty paired with a defensible competitive position.
And there was also a public vote, with thousands of members of our community of retail tech enthusiasts getting involved. Thanks to all those who took part! Based on the judging panel's feedback and the public vote, we then drew up our first ever RTIH Retail Technology Hot 100.
So, without further ado, here are the 100 hottest global retail technology ventures right now. Drum roll, please…
You can download the hot 100 in pdf format here, or flick through it here 👇👇👇 Enjoy!
Editor and Founder of Retail Technology Innovation Hub

items.body:
Asda fights crime, HMV sees double, Everseen sizzles: last month's most read retail technology articles
Check out our most clicked articles from August, including White Castle, Murphy USA, Focal Systems, UNIQLO, AutoStore, Amazon, Ocado Group, Lotte Shopping, and the RTIH Retail Technology Hot 100 List.
Everseen, Hanshow and OpenAI top first ever RTIH Retail Technology Hot 100 List
In partnership with 3D Cloud, RTIH is pleased to launch its first ever Retail Technology Hot 100 List. We’re bringing you the hottest companies whose solutions and systems are helping drive the retail sector forward.
These companies operate across the omnichannel retail landscape (stores, online, mobile, supply chain, payments etc).
Our judging panel, including Vineta Bajaj, Group CFO, Holland & Barrett, Dan McGrath, JD Group Customer Operations, JD Sports, Dr. Astha Purohit, Director of Product Management, Customer Data and Identity, Walmart, and Paula Bobbett, Chief Data and Digital Officer, Boots, provided feedback on those who have the most innovative, forward thinking technology offerings and are also best addressing retailers' current challenges, painpoints, and opportunities.
The judges used the following framework when making their picks:
1. Retailer problem fit - how meaningful, strategic, and widely felt the retailer pain being addressed is.
2. Production traction in retail (2025–2026) - real named retailer deployments, pilots. 
3. Innovation and defensibility - genuine technical novelty paired with a defensible competitive position. 
And there was also a public vote, with thousands of members of our community of retail tech enthusiasts getting involved. Thanks to all those who took part! Based on the judging panel's feedback and the public vote, we then drew up our first ever RTIH Retail Technology Hot 100.
So, without further ado, here are the 100 hottest global retail technology ventures right now. Drum roll, please…
White Castle onboard as launch partner as Murphy USA starts roll-out of autonomous hot food platform
Murphy USA, a retailer of gasoline and convenience merchandise with more than 1,800 stores located primarily in the Southwest, Southeast, Midwest and Northeast United States, has announced an initial roll-out of an autonomous foodservice platform in select larger format stores, providing customers another way to access hot, branded food. The platform, developed by Automated Retail Technologies (ART), will launch featuring hamburger chain White Castle.
“We’re continually evaluating opportunities that create additional value for our customers while building on the strengths that have made Murphy USA successful,” says Scott Woodward, Murphy USA Senior Vice President and Chief Merchandising Officer. “This relationship allows us to introduce a new convenience offering informed by customer insights, while maintaining the operational discipline and focus on everyday value. We’re encouraged by the opportunity to drive incremental inside sales, traffic and basket growth.”
“We’ve spent more than a century finding innovative ways to bring our Crave to customers wherever they are,” says Audra Mazzeo, White Castle Vice President of Retail Sales. “This partnership creates a unique opportunity to meet customers during their everyday routines and deliver the White Castle experience in a way that is convenient, fast, and incredibly tasty.”
Customers place orders through a touchscreen interface and receive hot food in approximately two minutes. Behind the scenes, ART’s technology automates preparation, heating, and delivery within a self-contained system. The technology is also designed as a modular, multi-brand platform capable of supporting nationally recognised brands, regional favorites and a variety of food categories over time.
Asda announces pilot across London stores of Auror crime reporting and intelligence technology
Asda is rolling out Auror, a crime reporting and intelligence platform. It says that a ten-week pilot in 30 London stores demonstrated the value of having a faster, more effective way to report incidents and identify repeat offenders in real-time.
According to the UK grocery retailer, the trial resulted in: more than £100,000 of products recovered and returned to shelves; 55% increase in crime prevention rates; 80% reduction in incident reporting time, from around 25 minutes to under five; improved identification of repeat and cross retailer offenders.
David Lepley, Chief Operating Officer at Asda, says: “Rolling out Auror across our estate will further strengthen our ability to prevent and tackle retail crime. The results from our London pilot demonstrated the value of having a faster and more effective way to report incidents and identify repeat offenders in real-time. By working more closely with police and retailers through a shared intelligence network, we can focus our efforts where they will have the greatest impact and help to tackle retail crime.”
Japanese fashion retailer UNIQLO lands at Canary Wharf retail and leisure destination in East London
Canary Wharf is getting a new addition to its fashion line-up with the arrival of UNIQLO.
Stuart Fyfe, Managing Director of Retail, Leisure and Hospitality at CWG, says: “We’re absolutely delighted to welcome UNIQLO to Canary Wharf. This is a brand that has built a global following by making exceptional quality feel effortless and accessible. UNIQLO joins a host of innovative, forward thinking brands that are redefining what a world class retail and leisure destination can feel like, and we couldn’t be more excited for them to be part of the story.”
“The momentum we’re seeing across the Wharf this year has been remarkable. Footfall continues to grow, our visitors are spending more time here and the energy across the retail, dining and leisure offer is palpable. UNIQLO aligns with our ambition and amplifies that energy. It’s another clear indication that Canary Wharf is one of London’s most exciting and dynamic destinations.”
UNIQLO follows a number of recent deals including Jigsaw, premium footwear retailer Nokwol, Sushi Dog, Holy Greens making its UK debut, Vagabond, The Tallyman and Bronson Burger. Sea Lanes Canary Wharf - an open air floating swimming pool - opened in June, welcoming more than 30,000 swimmers within the first month of opening.
99% of the estate’s retail and leisure space is currently occupied.
Ocado launches first automated customer fulfilment centre with Lotte Shopping in South Korea
Ocado Group reports the launch of its first customer fulfilment centre (CFC) with Lotte Shopping in South Korea. Following a partnership deal inked in 2022, last year Lotte went live with the Ocado Smart Platform, fulfilling orders using Ocado's in-store fulfilment (ISF) software. And now the first automated CFC will serve a catchment covering four million households across Busan and the broader Yeongnam region.
It also introduces a number of innovations for the first time. These include the launch of Ocado's fully automated freezer (Auto-Freezer), bringing Ocado's proprietary 'hive and bot' automation into temperatures as low as -25° C. The site will also support dawn delivery, enabling freshly packed grocery orders to reach customers’ homes before 7am.
It is also expected to be the most environmentally efficient Ocado CFC in the world, supporting a 100% electric vehicle fleet for daytime deliveries and operating more energy efficient 3D printed bots, with multi-temperature totes to maximise storage density for delivery. The widespread installation of solar panels will reduce annual carbon emissions by over 1,000 tonnes, those involved claim.
Vinyl loving HMV sees double at Bluewater Shopping Centre as retailer preps new store opening
Entertainment retailer HMV is moving on up at Bluewater Shopping Centre in the UK with a new two-storey store. It is poised to take over a 7,000 sq ft unit after Gravity Arcade shut down last month. A spokesperson for Gravity Arcade said that the premises were always intended to be a “temporary pop-up location”, which “operated for a limited period”.
The expanded store (double the size of HMV’s previous Bluewater location) will open later this year and stock vinyl, CDs, films, and TV shows, as well as T-shirts from major franchises including Star Wars, KPop Demon Hunters, and Funko POP! It will also offer a wide selection of books, from fiction and graphic novels to music biographies, young adult titles, and manga.
Phil Halliday, Managing Director at HMV and Fopp, says: "Bluewater has always been a key destination for the business, and we're thrilled to be expanding our footprint within the centre. Whether you're hunting down rare vinyl, diving into Manga, or picking up the latest merch, the new shop will offer something for everyone. We can't wait to welcome in customers later this year."
James Waugh, Centre Director at Bluewater, says: "As one of Bluewater's original retailers, having been with us since we first opened in 1999, HMV has always been a firm favourite with our guests. "Seeing them commit to an even bigger space is not only great news for us, but highlights a wider confidence in bricks and mortar retail. We look forward to seeing the new, larger store open its doors later this year."
The hmv delivers service will also be available, allowing people to order items not available in-store and have them delivered to their homes.
HMV currently operates more than 125 stores across the UK and Europe.
AutoStore announces deal with Amazon to supply automation technology products and solutions
There has been a lot of chatter this year about AutoStore and Amazon, the result of a jobs posting by the latter seeking staff with experience of the former. And now we have an official announcement.
The pair have shaken hands on an agreement that establishes a framework for the supply of AutoStore’s products and solutions to Amazon on a global basis. Whilst the agreement defines the terms for further procurement of AutoStore systems by Amazon, it does not contain any purchasing commitments at this time, a press release notes.
While this will no doubt boost AutoStore's share price, it should be noted that Amazon has announced similar agreements in the past, for example with Balyo, which did not result in significant sales. Balyo was taken private in 2026 by SoftBank Group Corp. which also remains a significant shareholder in AutoStore (and various others).
Village Super Market tests out new Focal Systems computer vision powered inventory technology
Focal Systems, an AI powered retail technology company specialising in computer vision and shelf intelligence, has announced Top Stock, a module that gives retailers automatic, hourly visibility into inventory stored above the shelf line, without store associate audits, ladder climbs, or manual scanning.
During a one-month pilot, Village Supermarkets says it achieved:
- $24,000 in previously unaccounted for inventory identified and recovered in the first month
- 75% reduction in weekly audit labour, from four hours to just one hour
- Ten hours saved weekly on the night crew
- 36% reduction in top stock inventory
- 1% on-shelf availability improvement across test store, on top of an existing Focal driven baseline of 97%, where marginal gains at that level translate to hundreds of thousands in incremental annual sales
- Increased day crew replenishment rates and planogram compliance

E-commerce specialist Aaron West leaves Ticketmaster and heads to German fast food chain Burgermeister
Burgermeister has appointed Aaron West as Digital Growth Manager. He joins from Ticketmaster Deutschland, where he served as Senior E-commerce Manager, and his CV also includes stints at ShopFabrik and Shoepassion Group.
In a LinkedIn post, he said: “I'm putting on a new hat: Digital Growth Manager at Burgermeister. It’s not a new personality, and it's definitely not a title I need to hide behind. I'm still the same person who gets curious, tests things, builds systems, and tries to figure out what actually moves growth forward. The only difference is that now, experimentation and building new solutions aren't just side quests, they're the core mission. And the stage is Burgermeister.”
He added: “I was a customer here long before I joined the team, which matters a lot to me. Quality isn't just something you communicate in an ad; it's something people taste under the U-Bahn, remember, and come back for. Burgermeister is expanding fast across Germany and internationally, which is the exact kind of growth moment I love. Scaling isn't just about opening more locations. It's about keeping the brand sharp while the digital machinery gets bigger: customer journeys, CRM, automation, local demand, and everything in between.”
West concluded: “My focus will be helping the brand grow digitally without losing what makes it unique. I like to take vague growth problems and make them visible, testable, and useful. Same curiosity, same builder mindset. New hat, bigger playground. Let's go.”

Health and beauty retailer Bodycare will open the doors to its third Studio Store at Highcross Leicester on Saturday 5th September. This builds on launches in Sheffield and Derby.

What makes this homecoming even more special though, is that we’re welcoming back some familiar faces to the store team from Bodycare’s previous time with us. items.body:
EE offers families free in-store ‘Parents Evening’ online safety sessions ahead of new school year
EE is bringing ‘Parents’ Evening’ sessions to the high street for parents amid back to school season. The one to one bookable appointments have been designed to help families manage young people’s online safety and social media use. This builds on support already offered to young people, including Safer SIMs and smartphone guidance.
It comes as millions of families across the UK prepare for a return to school this week. EE says it is aiming to set the stage for a national conversation between parents and teachers about smartphone safety. Smartphone ownership is now the norm among secondary school children, with nine in ten expected to walk through the school gates with one in their pocket this week. But new research from EE finds parents, teachers and pupils are all expecting fallout from a summer of out of school screentime to spill into the classroom this term and are calling for help making the return to routine easier.
Nine in ten secondary school teachers have seen concentration spans shorten in recent years. A further 85% are seeing issues originating online, from group chat fallouts to late night scrolling, routinely disrupt lessons and eat into valuable learning time. It’s a challenge most pronounced in the weeks after the summer holidays. Two in five teachers say re-establishing phone rules and expectations with pupils in the first few weeks of term is significantly harder than at any other point in the year.
Matthew Burton, Headteacher of Thornhill Community Academy and star of Channel 4's Educating Yorkshire, says: "Establishing good routines after a long summer holiday is crucial. We often see pupils come back to school after six weeks of relative freedom online and land with a bump at their school desk. For teachers, a lot of the first half of term is spent getting pupils to shake those bad habits and refocus on their studies.”
“This isn’t about demonising parents for letting kids use smart devices; with the right guardrails they can be an invaluable resource. But as a parent myself I know that the conversations that make the biggest difference happen at the kitchen table, so I wanted this homework sheet to give parents some genuinely useful tips to give their children the best possible start to the new school year."
At home, the picture is similar. 72% of pupils say smartphones and social media have led to arguments with their parents this summer, and a third of parents say the return to school adds further pressure as children readjust after heavier than usual screen use. For parents, the concern is as much about promoting safe use as it is curbing over-use. 31% are concerned that their child is experiencing negative or harmful content online.
For 55%, the pace of technological change is overwhelming, making it difficult to judge whether they are setting the right rules at home. 52% state that dedicated sessions on children's online safety would help them navigate the period.
Claire Gillies, CEO, Consumer at BT’s Consumer Division, comments: "The digital world brings huge opportunities for young people, but it can also be a source of anxiety for parents. As a parent of a teenager myself, I understand those challenges firsthand. That’s why we’re committed to giving families practical support and trusted advice when they need it most.”
“As the UK’s best network for families, we are committed to helping people stay connected with confidence. From our ‘Parents Evening’ sessions to Safer SIMs and smartphone guidance, EE is helping families make informed decisions as children head back to school. We’ve made tens of thousands of appointments available in our stores nationwide, and I encourage parents to take advantage of that support.”
Throughout September, free half hour online safety appointments will be available in EE stores nationwide, giving parents one to one time with a trained colleague to set up parental controls, review app settings and talk through the questions they are not sure how to ask. The sessions will also be available throughout the academic year, so parents can book in a refresher session every term.
EE has also worked with Matthew Burton, alongside teachers from across the country, to create a free 'homework sheet' for parents. The ten-minute exercise is designed to help parents start the conversation and set up effective parental controls before the new term gets under way.
Rachel Huggins, CEO at Internet Matters, says: “Many parents tell us they feel overwhelmed when it comes to their children’s online safety and that managing children’s screentime can feel like a constant battle. After a summer of changed routines and often increased screen use, the start of a new school year can be an ideal opportunity for families to reset digital habits and expectations together.”
“One of the best places to start is with open and honest family conversations. Taking an interest in children's online lives, discussing why boundaries and balance on screen use are important and making sure they know they won't be blamed if something goes wrong can help create the trust they need to seek support when it matters most. The EE homework sheet is a useful way to help parents kick-start those conversations, while EE's Parents' Evenings make it easier for busy families to access practical support on parental controls and online safety settings. Conversations and controls go hand in hand, and together they can help children enjoy the benefits of the digital world safely and confidently.”

He added: “This year’s submissions have without doubt been our best yet. To quote one of the judges: The examples of innovative developments across both traditional and digital retail spaces were truly remarkable.”

The campaign will focus on lululemon’s major European markets, including Germany, Switzerland and the Netherlands, and will also run in Poland, where the brand entered earlier this year, and Austria, where lululemon will arrive for the first time later this week with an opening on Vienna’s prestigious Kärntner 
“Zalando is our biggest retail partner across Europe, and as we continue to expand our physical and digital reach across the region, they are an important part of how we reach more guests across key markets,” said Sarah Clark, Senior Vice President, EMEA, lululemon. “Across lululemon’s presence in EMEA, Germany has the largest share of online purchases and so we know that our local guest is keen to buy our apparel online. Giving them the chance to buy through Zalando before the wider collection arrives in our stores gives us another way to meet our German guests through the channels where they already choose to shop.”
Clark added, “This collaboration also builds on our ongoing commitment to building a community with Zalando around our brand. This has included hosting a series of events for our guests to connect in real life through experiences such as our Greet the Sun activation last year featuring renowned singer and songwriter Kim Petras and our upcoming recovery lounge at the Berlin Marathon later this month.”
lululemon has stores and a digital presence in 23 markets across EMEA through a mix of company and franchised operated locations. The company remains focused on strategically expanding across EMEA to reach new guests and has entered four new markets, Poland, Hungary, Romania and Greece, and adds Austria and India in the coming weeks.

items.title: Retail giants including M&S and Tesco warn Burnham's business rates raid could drive up cost of living
items.summary: Some of Britain's biggest chains have united to warn the new Prime Minister against piling higher taxes on their shops in order to pay for lower bills for pubs and music venues.
items.body:
Retail giants including M&S and Tesco warn Burnham's business rates raid could drive up cost of living
- See more This is Money on Google - save us as a Preferred Source
Retailers including Marks & Spencer and Tesco have warned Andy Burnham that a business rates raid could drive up the cost of living, as well as hitting jobs and investment at large stores.
Some of Britain's biggest chains have united to warn the new Prime Minister against piling higher taxes on their shops in order to pay for lower bills for other businesses such as pubs.
Shops should not have to pay more, according to Marks & Spencer, Tesco, Sainsbury's, B&Q-owner Kingfisher, Morrisons, Primark and Asda.
The letter was also signed by Usdaw, the Union of Shop, Distributive and Allied Workers, which has around 370,000 members.
In a letter sent by the Retail Jobs Alliance, big firms have said future changes 'should support continued investment by bricks-and-mortar retailers across the country.'
It said high street retailers had to grapple with a total of £7bn in extra costs and taxes last year, including business rates, packaging levies and higher wages.
The coalition warned that these factors were a 'direct cost driver on prices' and said increasing them further would drive up the cost of goods for customers.
'Further increases would place even greater pressure on retailers' ability to support customers through competitive pricing and cost of living initiatives,' the letter said.
'Retail stores are integral to [the] high street renaissance but they cannot continue investing in communities if they face an ever-increasing tax burden.'
It comes as the Prime Minister and Chancellor, John Healey prepare their first Budget for 28 October.
Budget plea: Major retailers have asked Andy Burnham to exempt them from higher taxes
The letter went on to say that businesses including pubs and restaurants 'all rely on vibrant town centres with strong footfall and consumer spending,' which big shops help to create.
By cutting rates for hospitality and increasing costs for retail, the High Street 'ecosystem' is at risk and the wider benefits of helping venues 'will inevitably be reduced,' it added.
Business rates are paid on the rateable value of a commercial property, based on its estimated rental value, as well as 'multiplier' rates based on property size.
Labour has already announced it will give pubs and music venues a 20 per cent discount off their rates bills from next spring, as well as ordering a consultation into the way pub and hotel business rates bills are calculated.
It promised in its manifesto to 'level the playing field between the High Street and online giants'.
There are concerns ahead of the Budget that premises with rateable values of above £500,000 will have to pay more from next spring.
A higher 'multipler' was introduced last year for this band of properties, which includes big department stores and supermarkets as well as online warehouses.
The retailers have now asked to exempt all bricks-and-mortar retail stores from the higher multiplier.
This summer's record heatwaves have created fresh concerns over food prices over the next few months while retailers and food producers are also experiencing increases to their energy bills.
Higher rates would also 'severely impact investment, employment and the viability of these anchor stores across the country.'
The latest worrying youth unemployment figures last week revealed that 981,000 people aged 16 to 24 were not 'earning or learning' between April and June.
Exempting shops would 'support your commitment to growth in every postcode by safeguarding retail employment across the country, the foundation that makes vibrant high streets and communities possible,' the letter concluded.

items.title: HMRC reminds retailers to prepare for Vaping Products Duty, starting 1 October
items.summary: With one month to go until the start of Vaping Products Duty and the Vaping Duty Stamps Scheme, HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) is reminding businesses across the vaping supply chain, including retailers and wholesalers, to prepare for the changes. The new excise duty of… This story continues at HMRC reminds retailers to prepare for Vaping Products Duty, starting 1 October Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
The new excise duty of £2.20 per 10ml on vaping products, whether they contain nicotine or not, will come into force alongside tobacco duty increases.
Together, they form part of the government’s wider plans to create a smoke-free generation, tackle youth vaping and help adult smokers to give up tobacco.
HMRC said Retailers and wholesalers should work with their suppliers to ensure the vaping products they stock comply with the new requirements.
Those that only sell or distribute duty-paid vaping products wholesale or retail, do not need to apply for Vaping Products Duty or Vaping Duty Stamps Scheme approval.
They can continue to buy and sell existing eligible unstamped stock during a six-month transition period from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027.
However, vaping products manufactured in, or imported into, the UK on or after 1 October 2026 must have a duty stamp.
From 1 April 2027, the retail packaging of all vaping products sold or supplied in the UK must carry a valid vaping duty stamp. Businesses that do not comply with the new rules may face civil or criminal sanctions.
Further detail for those who sell, store, distribute or handle vaping products by wholesale or retail in the UK is available.
Consumers in the UK will begin to see changes to vaping products and packaging from 1 October 2026, as Vaping Products Duty and the Vaping Duty Stamps Scheme come into effect. HMRC said it will provide further information to help them understand the changes.

items.title: Tesco and M&S warn Burnham against Budget tax raid on retailers
items.summary: Top supermarkets including Tesco, Sainsbury’s and Marks & Spencer have urged Andy Burnham to rule out a Budget tax raid on retailers, warning they are already facing “unsustainable” costs. The Retail Jobs Alliance (RJA), which represents retailers employing more than 1m people, has urged the Prime Minister not to prioritise pubs and bars over high [...]
items.body:
Tesco and M&S warn Burnham against Budget tax raid on retailers
Top supermarkets including Tesco, Sainsbury’s and Marks & Spencer have urged Andy Burnham to rule out a Budget tax raid on retailers, warning they are already facing “unsustainable” costs.
The Retail Jobs Alliance (RJA), which represents retailers employing more than 1m people, has urged the Prime Minister not to prioritise pubs and bars over high street retailers.
Burnham has committed to easing the business rates burden facing pubs, bars and live music venues, as part of his pledge to rejuvenate British high streets.
But these commitments have sparked fears that the government could hike the business rates burden facing bigger retailers in order to balance the books.
The letter, seen by City AM, warns Burnham against hiking the business rates multiplier for stores with a rateable value of more than £500,000.
The RJA wrote: “We welcome your commitment to ‘growth in every postcode’ and support the recent announcement to reduce business rates for pubs, clubs and live music venues, alongside measures to review reliefs for businesses that do not make a positive contribution to local communities.
“Retail stores are integral to high street renaissance but they cannot continue investing in communities if they face an ever-increasing tax burden.”
The retailers claim that footfall for hospitality businesses would “inevitably be reduced” if a hike to business rates eradicates retailers from the high street.
“The high street is a single ecosystem. Pubs, restaurants, retailers and other local businesses all rely on vibrant town centres with strong footfall and consumer spending. Reducing business rates for hospitality while increasing costs for retail risks weakening that ecosystem,” the RJA told the Prime Minister.
Business rates ‘driving up prices’
The trade body said retail is already the UK’s most-taxed sector compared to its economist output. The sector pays 21 per cent of all business rates though it represents only five per cent of GDP, it said.
The £7bn which was added to retail’s cost burden at last year’s Budget is a “direct cost driver on prices,” the retailers told the Prime Minister.
“Further increases would place even greater pressure on retailers’ ability to support customers through competitive pricing and cost of living initiatives, while continuing to offer employment opportunities in communities across the country,” the group added.
The RJA also represents Primark, Morrisons and B&Q-owner Kingfisher. Its letter was backed by Usdaw, the UK’s fifth-largest trade union.
The retailers called on Burnham to exempt all brick-and-mortar retailers from the highest business rates multiplier, which currently stands at 50.8p.
“This would support your commitment to growth in every postcode by safeguarding retail employment across the country, the foundation that makes vibrant high streets and communities possible,” they said.
Burnham has already faced calls to exempt high-street retailers from business rates rises. The Real Rates Reform Alliance has told the government to hike taxes on online sales to pay for a 37 per cent tax cut for brick-and-mortar shops.
Last month, a host of industry bodies accused Burnham of taking a “piecemeal” approach to business rates reform after announcing a review into the fairness of the system for pubs and hotels.
Days into his tenure as Prime Minister, Burnham announced a 20 per cent cut to the business rates bill of all pubs in the UK.

items.title: SNP slammed for ‘mind-boggling’ food price cap plans
items.summary: The Scottish government has been criticised for its “mind-boggling” plans to impose price caps on major retailers operating in the country, including Tesco, Sainsbury’s and Aldi.  The Scottish National Party (SNP) has published a draft bill for the policy, which has been dismissed as an “unnecessary exercise” by leading retailers.  SNP leader John Swinney’s initial [...]
items.body:
SNP slammed for ‘mind-boggling’ food price cap plans
The Scottish government has been criticised for its “mind-boggling” plans to impose price caps on major retailers operating in the country, including Tesco, Sainsbury’s and Aldi.
The Scottish National Party (SNP) has published a draft bill for the policy, which has been dismissed as an “unnecessary exercise” by leading retailers.
SNP leader John Swinney’s initial announcement of the plans was swiftly followed by reports that then-Chancellor Rachel Reeves was considering voluntary price caps for grocers in England.
Reeves quickly abandoned the policy – which Marks & Spencer boss Stuart Machin dubbed “completely preposterous” – but the Scottish government looks set to plough ahead with the regime.
The draft bill has set out plans to introduce “statutory price ceilings” for up to 50 essential food items, including bread, milk and eggs.
“Whilst food price inflation has eased from recent peaks, many households continue to face challenges affording essential food items, and it is possible we could face future high inflation,” the draft legislation claims.
The new laws would require large supermarkets to price a product in each capped category at or below the government-set level.
If this product runs out, grocers would be required to replace it with another product in the same category at the capped price – regardless of its original price point.
Grocers are not required to provide price-capped products in categories which they do not normally stock, meaning supermarkets could be incentivised to stop offering essential foods to avoid losing money.
“There is recognition that the proposed approach may simply mean that retailers affected choose not to stock a specific item that is subject to a price cap,” the draft bill concedes.
Price caps ‘will force shortages’
The Scottish Retail Consortium (SRC), which represents leading grocers, said the sample legislation “show[s] how fiendishly complex, costly, and onerous this unnecessary exercise will be if implemented”.
The trade body criticised the SNP for failing to specify which products will be capped, what the prices will be, or to provide detail on how it will support producers in offering cheaper imports.
“Ironically one element the paper does confirm is that we have a robust competitive grocery market – which Ministers don’t seem to recognise obviates the need for statutory price caps in the first place,” the SRC added.
Clive Black, an analyst at Shore Capital, told City AM: “If the Scottish Government wants to send a message to the food and wider industries of ‘do not invest in Scotland’, then introducing minimum food prices is one of them.”
In the draft bill, the SNP said that it could hit grocers with unlimited fines for high-level convictions relating to the new laws, or penalties of up to £10,000 for lower-level breaches.
The Scottish government’s own lawyers have told Swinney that the price-cap regime may be unlawful, as reported by the Scottish Sun.
Dr Chris Snowdon, head of lifestyle economics at the Institute of Economic Affairs, said: “John Swinney is a latter-day King Canute hopelessly trying to stop the rising tide of inflation. As surely as night follows day, price caps lead to shortages on the shelves and the sale of inferior products.
“At some point in the near future, the SNP’s price caps will require supermarkets to sell products at a loss, which they will not do, and shoppers will soon find that they can’t buy them at all.”

items.title: Ikea cuts prices as customers struggle with rising cost of living
items.summary: The Swedish retailer has seen revenue decline as the rising cost of living reduces people's ability to buy new furniture.
items.body:
Ikea cuts prices as customers struggle with rising cost of living
- Published
Swedish furniture giant Ikea is cutting prices across hundreds of products in Europe to woo customers struggling with deepening cost-of-living pressures.
Ikea has seen revenue decline over the past two years as the rising cost of living reduces people's ability to invest in new furniture and home renovations.
The company is spending â¬1.2bn (Â£1bn) on the price cuts to items including the Billy bookcase and Kallax storage units, with reductions of up to 28% on certain products.
Ikea said it could make the cuts by making savings throughout the supply chain, such as packaging costs, but acknowledged profits may take a hit.
Ingka, the franchisee which operates most of Ikea's European stores, said the cuts were "not an activity or short-term campaign".
"It's about making IKEA more affordable when people need it most, even if it means accepting a lower margin," said Juvencio Maeztu, chief executive of Ingka. "The cost of living is increasing and it's getting tougher and tougher for many people."
He added: "For many people, home is a bedroom in a shared house, and it's even more important to offer storage and organised solutions."
Ikea has reduced its prices several times in recent years, even as it caused a hit to the company's revenue and profit in its most recent earnings report.
The latest specific reductions vary slightly by country. Price cuts for British customers include the Kallax shelving unit going from Â£60 to Â£49 and the Billy bookcase being cut by Â£10 to Â£25.
Ikea is also trying to attract new customers by opening smaller stores in central areas, such as London's Oxford Street and Churchill Square in Brighton.
In 2024 it launched its own second-hand online marketplace in a bid to rival sites like eBay and Facebook Marketplace.
Despite a recent uptick, consumer confidence in Europe is at its lowest level for almost three years due to concerns about inflation and the cost of living, according to EU figures. , external
British consumers, meanwhile, are becoming more optimistic about the economy and their own finances, following a truce in the Middle East, but analysts have warned that inflation and the rising cost of living could dent consumer confidence in the coming months.
Ikea operates over 500 stores worldwide under a franchise system.
Many of its minimalist, self-assembled products have become ubiquitous in homes across Europe.
But it has faced criticism from environmentalists for contributing to a culture of disposable furniture and excess packaging.

items.title: UK DRS: what retailers and wholesalers need to be asking suppliers now | Viewpoint: Bill Power
items.summary: Confirmation of the Producer Fee will give drinks suppliers greater clarity over DRS costs. For retailers and wholesalers, it heralds critical conversations with suppliers about price, terms, deposits, product changes and stock The UK Deposit Return Scheme (DRS) Producer Fee will matter most directly to… This story continues at UK DRS: what retailers and wholesalers need to be asking suppliers now | Viewpoint: Bill Power Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
For retailers and wholesalers, it heralds critical conversations with suppliers about price, terms, deposits, product changes and stock
The UK Deposit Return Scheme (DRS) Producer Fee will matter most directly to drinks producers and importers. But its confirmation should also matter to their retail and wholesale customers.
Many suppliers will already have been modelling possible DRS costs. A confirmed fee gives them greater certainty over one of the significant costs they will face when the scheme goes live in October 2027.
For retailers and wholesalers, the question is what happens next:
* How will suppliers reflect DRS costs in their pricing?
* What could this mean for customer terms and promotions?
* Are products, packs or barcodes changing?
* When will DRS-ready stock start arriving?
* Are both sides ready for the deposit to move through ordering, invoicing and payment?
These are not questions to leave until 2027. Confirmation of the Producer Fee will allow suppliers to model their DRS costs with greater certainty. What is not determined is how individual businesses will manage those costs.
How suppliers manage or recover those costs may differ by product, customer and channel. Retailers and wholesalers need to understand what their suppliers are proposing early enough to assess the implications for pricing, customer terms, promotions, price-marked packs and other commercial arrangements.
Cost is only part of the supplier conversation. Retailers and wholesalers also need early visibility of changes suppliers are planning ahead of DRS, including pack materials, sizes or formats, barcodes, artwork and product data.
Changes to pack format, size, barcodes or artwork can affect ranging, shelf space, warehousing and stock planning. Retailers and wholesalers need to know what is changing, when revised products will enter the supply chain and how existing stock will be managed around go-live.
The 20p deposit is separate from the Producer Fee, but creates its own commercial, accounting and systems questions.
Retailers and wholesalers will pay deposits when purchasing in-scope drinks and charge them when those products are sold on. That creates potential cash-flow implications and raises questions about whether existing credit terms remain appropriate.
There is also an important VAT distinction. Under HMRC’s proposed approach, businesses in the supply chain will not account for VAT on the deposit itself. VAT on deposits that are not refunded would instead be accounted for by the scheme administrator.
Retailers, wholesalers and suppliers therefore need to make sure the different treatment of the product and deposit is understood and reflected correctly through invoicing, payments and the systems supporting them.
Confirmation of the Producer Fee is a useful point for retailers and wholesalers to get specific information about key suppliers: what is changing, when it is changing and what that means for price, terms, deposits, products and stock.
Identifying those issues now gives both sides more time to resolve them before UK DRS goes live in October 2027.
Bill Power is Chairman of DRS International

items.title: Abu Bakr introduces low-price back-to-school hot meals, snacks and drinks

The new menu will be available from the Food 2 Go counters in every Abu Bakr… This story continues at Abu Bakr introduces low-price back-to-school hot meals, snacks and drinks Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
The new menu will be available from the Food 2 Go counters in every Abu Bakr Supermarket store across Leeds and Batley, with the family-run retailer saying the range has been created to offer quick, filling and value-for-money options for busy parents and schoolchildren alike.
The offer starts at just £1.50, with customers able to pick up two freshly made samosas for only £1.50 or a hot pasty for £1.50, making it one of the supermarket’s most affordable freshly prepared food ranges for families.
The launch builds on Abu Bakr’s growing Food 2 Go brand, which has become one of the supermarket chain’s fastest-growing fresh food offerings.
The new school meal range includes:
| Meal | Price | 
| Two freshly made samosas (including vegetarian options) | £1.50 | 
| One hot pasty (including vegetarian options) | £1.50 | 
| Butter Chicken or Chicken Tikka Masala, with a choice of meat and vegetarian curry alternatives | £7.50 | 
| Freshly made warm naan bread | £1.00 | 
| Two cans of Coke or a selection of fresh juice drinks | £1.00 | 
The meals have been designed so customers can mix and match snacks, drinks and hot food, making the range ideal for school lunches, after-school meals or an affordable family dinner.
Abu Bakr Supermarket said the launch comes at a time when many parents are looking for affordable food options during the expensive back-to-school period.
Managing director Hamza Hussain said the retailer wanted to combine convenience with quality while keeping prices accessible.
“Back to school is one of the busiest and most expensive times of the year for families, so we wanted Food 2 Go to offer something that’s fresh, filling and genuinely affordable, said Hussain.
“Our new kids meal range has been created for busy parents and hungry children who want quality food without paying takeaway prices.
“Whether it’s a couple of samosas after school, a hot pasty on the go, or a Butter Chicken or Chicken Tikka Masala that the family can enjoy at home, we’ve made sure there’s something for everyone and every budget.
“The best part is that every single Abu Bakr store will now offer these meals through our Food 2 Go counters, giving customers the same great choice wherever they shop.”
The new kids meal range will be available across Abu Bakr Supermarket stores in Queens Road, Roundhay Road, Dewsbury Road, Kirkstall Road and Batley.
With Abu Bakr continuing its rapid expansion across Yorkshire, the supermarket said Food 2 Go will remain a major part of its investment in affordable, freshly prepared meals for local communities.

items.body:
It is working with suppliers to support KeyStore retailers as they strengthen relationships with customers and local communities through the KeyStore Community Fund.
In a collaboration with PepsiCo, retailer Bikram Kaur – who owns KeyStore Burns Square in Greenock – presented £900 for the purchase of new team kits to Greenock Juniors Football Club, a local team whose players shop regularly in the store and are well known in the community.
Bikram Kaur, who welcomed Steve Keegan of Greenock Juniors FC to his store to present the cheque, said: “It makes a great difference, being relatively new in the area, to be able to give back to the community. It helps us build relationships in our neighbourhood, so we’re delighted to be supported by PepsiCo and the KeyStore Community Fund to top up our donation to support the club.”
Saying how grateful the club is for KeyStore’s sponsorship, Keegan commented: “It can be difficult in this area to get backing from local businesses, but when we approached KeyStore, their willingness to invest in the team shows how much they care about the local community.
“Bikram has been a great help, and the team will continue to be loyal customers of KeyStore Burns Square.”
Katie Dempster, group marketing manager at Filshill, said: “We’ve had a great summer of football, and KeyStore retailers have grasped the opportunity to collaborate with our suppliers to raise awareness of both the KeyStore and Filshill brands.
“Bikram’s tie-up with Greenock Juniors FC is a prime example of how the KeyStore Community Fund can help our customers get involved with grassroots and local football teams, building relationships and supporting people who shop in their stores every week.
“Our summer of football activity has also reaffirmed our commitment to leveraging partnerships to provide promotions, pricing and range support to drive our retailers’ store performance, tapping into our ‘five reasons to join KeyStore’ campaign: delivery, social media support, KeyStore Community Fund, proven core range, and real business support.”

items.summary: Discover what's happening in retail today, Retail Times publishes international & UK retail news covering products, data, tech, packaging, people, research, comment and much more.
