Pregnant women and young children will be amongst the first eligible for the NHS flu vaccination. Despite a small increase in uptake, the NHS reports that more than […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
Boots will start delivering the first wave of NHS flu vaccinations for eligible cohorts from 1 September, helping to protect those most at risk ahead of the flu season.
Pregnant women and young children will be amongst the first eligible for the NHS flu vaccination. Despite a small increase in uptake, the NHS reports that more than half of pregnant women did not receive a flu vaccination during the last year’s flu season.
Flu can cause severe illness, particularly in vulnerable groups such as pregnant women, older adults, young children, and those with underlying health conditions. Data from the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) highlights the effectiveness of the seasonal jab, showing that flu vaccinations significantly reduced the risk of hospitalisation by up to 40% in adults aged 65 and over during last year’s flu season.
New research from Boots suggests that Brits are using autumn and the return of routine as an opportunity to prioritise their health, with 44% of Brits agreeing that September is up there as the ideal time for a reset. For a third (32%), the biggest driver for making healthier changes at this time is seeking to futureproof their wellbeing before winter sets in.
Similarly, Boots also reports a 20% increase YoY across flu jab bookings, suggesting Brits are thinking even earlier about immunity this year and before winter hits.
Claire Nevinson, Superintendent Pharmacist at Boots, said: “With summer coming to an end, customers are already thinking about protecting themselves ahead of the flu season. Flu can make people feel very unwell and may pose a serious risk to those considered to be vulnerable. It’s a good idea to plan ahead and ensure you have your flu jab as early as possible to help protect yourself and those around you from flu and reduce the risk of passing the virus to others this winter.”
From 22 September, the Boots Private Winter Flu Jab service*** will be available in many Boots stores. Following this, on 1 October the wider roll out of the NHS flu vaccination will be made available to all eligible adult groups, including those aged 65 and over and adults aged 18 to 64 with certain long-term health conditions. The NHS childhood flu vaccination will be available in over 140 selected Boots stores.
Customers can book an appointment, check eligibility, view local store availability, or book an appointment at boots.com or speak with a team member at your local Boots pharmacy.
To help patients make informed decisions about their seasonal healthcare, Claire Nevinson answers five common questions:
- Does the flu jab give you flu?
“No, the flu vaccination contains a tiny amount of an inactive flu virus that cannot give you the flu. Some people may experience a temporary raised temperature and aching muscles, and you may feel sore at the injection site, but these side effects tend to be mild and only last for a day or so.”
- Can pregnant women get the flu vaccination?
“Yes, the flu jab is suitable and recommended at any stage of pregnancy, from the early weeks through to delivery. Pregnancy naturally alters how the body responds to infections, placing expectant mothers at higher risk of complications. Vaccination helps protect both mother and baby, passing on vital immunity during the baby’s first few months of life.”
- When should you get the flu vaccination?
“The best time to have a flu jab to ensure maximum protection is in the autumn months before the virus becomes more prevalent. This allows the body to obtain optimum protection. After you’ve received the jab, it usually takes around 10 to 14 days for optimum protection so it’s best to book your vaccination as early as you can.”
- Do you only need a flu vaccination only once in your life?
“No, protection from the flu vaccination declines with time and the types of flu virus in circulation change so the vaccination is updated each year. This is why it’s important to get the flu vaccination every year.”
- Does the flu vaccination have side effects?
“Yes, like any vaccination, it is normal to experience mild side effects after receiving a flu vaccination. These side effects are a result of your body’s natural immune response as it builds protection against the flu virus. The most common side effects, such as a sore arm, fever or fatigue are generally mild and tend to resolve within one to two days. To help your body recover and ease any discomfort, you can consider taking paracetamol if it’s suitable for you, stay well-hydrated, and ensure you get plenty of rest.”

items.body:
Majestic, the UK’s largest specialist wine retailer, has kicked off a six-week festival of fundraising in a bid to raise tens of thousands of pounds for the Majestic Charitable Foundation.
Teams from across the business will pull together to raise funds in a variety of different ways throughout September and early October as part of its Small Majestic Acts campaign, proving that small gestures from colleagues, customers and suppliers can add up to make a big impact.
Each of Majestic’s 217 stores will host its own Charity Tasting during the campaign, with proceeds from ticket sales going directly to the Majestic Charitable Foundation. Stores will also be giving customers the chance to donate 25p at the checkout through Majestic’s partnership with fintech charity Pennies. Since that tie-up was launched back in December 2024, 1.1 million Majestic shoppers have raised more than £260,000 by adding a charity donation at the till – and store colleagues will be encouraging even more customers to start the giving habit during Micro-Donation Week, which runs until Sunday 6th September.
Majestic will host its annual Charity Golf Day on Thursday 8th October, while colleagues will also tackle a host of personal challenges in support of the Foundation and its three national charity partners: The Brain Tumour Charity, Campaign Against Living Miserably (CALM) and Child Bereavement UK – all of which were nominated by Majestic colleagues.
One of Majestic’s key producer partners, Felix Solis, has already pledged to donate £10,000 to the campaign to mark the 10th birthday of The Guv’nor – Majestic’s best-selling red wine. And Majestic is now urging as many customers and producers as possible to complete their own Small Majestic Acts during the next six weeks, to help make a huge difference to families in need across the UK.
The fundraising campaign comes a year after Majestic celebrated its 45th birthday with its epic Majestic Miles challenge. Colleagues covered a combined total of 45,000 miles in the space of just 45 days by walking, running, hiking, cycling, rowing, kayaking and roller blading across all four corners of the country. Majestic has a long and proud history of philanthropy, having raised more than £1million for charity prior to the launch of the Majestic Charitable Foundation in 2024.
Jacqui Rouse, group people director at Majestic Wine Group and Trustee of the Majestic Charitable Foundation, said: “Our colleagues are incredibly passionate about supporting causes close to their hearts, and so we’re all really excited to get started with this year’s dedicated fundraising campaign.
“Times are tough for a lot of people right now, but thousands of Small Majestic Acts from our friends, family, colleagues, customers and suppliers over the next few weeks can add up to make a massive difference for our incredible charity partners. Whether it’s something as little as adding a 25p charity donation when you pay by card in a Majestic store, donating to our Just Giving page, or running a marathon, the support of the Majestic family will help us have a huge impact in the communities we serve.”

Sales data from Co-op’s pop-up stores at Download Festival, Sky presents the Isle of Wight Festival, […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! items.body:
Festivalgoers in 2026 are increasingly choosing healthier food and drink options, according to new sales data from Co-op, with fresh fruit, nutritious snacks, water and functional drinks rising in popularity at the convenience retailer’s pop-up festival stores this summer.
Sales data from Co-op’s pop-up stores at Download Festival, Sky presents the Isle of Wight Festival, Klarna Presents Latitude Festival, Kendal Calling and Belladrum Festival, has uncovered that music fans are turning into five-a-day festivalgoers and packing more fresh fruit into their weekends than ever before.
Set against the backdrop of a scorching summer, overall fresh food purchases at festival stores are up 26 percent compared to last year, while sales of grapes and stone fruits climbed 38 percent. Demand for Co-op fruit juices increased by 20 percent, Co-op fruit pot sales rose by 11 percent and Co-op Fairtrade bananas increased eight percent, suggesting festivalgoers are being more conscious of getting their five-a-day when partying in the fields.
In response to this trend, the Co-op increased orders of grapes by 34 percent, bananas by 26 percent, fresh juices by 26 percent, apples by 25 percent and soft fruits by 21 percent for its pop-up stores at Pepsi Max Presents Creamfields Festival and Pepsi Max Presents Reading & Leeds Festivals at the weekend.
Co-op own brand still water is the number one selling drink and is among the top two overall selling products at every Co-op pop-up store across the five festivals to date. Shoppers have purchased more than 7,000 gallons of Co-op still water at festival stores this summer, helping festivalgoers stay hydrated while also supporting clean water and sanitation projects in some of the world’s poorest communities through Co-op’s partnership with The One Foundation – Co-op donates 3p for every litre of own-brand water sold to the charity.
Another success story of the summer has been Co-op’s new range of vitamin waters, which have quickly found a fanbase among festivalgoers looking for hydration and functional benefits such as muscle maintenance and recovery, digestive wellbeing and electrolyte replenishment.
So far this festival season, Co-op has sold the equivalent of 1,600 litres of its new vitamin water range across its festival stores. To meet this demand, Co-op increased orders by 150% for the August weekend’s festivals compared with the first event of the summer.
Georgina Coley, festivals partnership manager at Co-op, said: “Festival weekends are all about having a good time, but it’s clear that people don’t want to leave their healthy habits at home. Our sales data has uncovered the trend for festivalgoers making more balanced choices across the weekend, whether it’s picking up fresh fruit for breakfast, grabbing a juice before heading to the main stage, or stocking up on healthy snacks for the day ahead.”
Co-op’s festival pop-up stores have been helping music fans stock up on everything they need for a weekend in the fields since 2018. Bringing the convenience of a local Co-op store to some of the UK’s biggest festivals, the shops offer a wide range of food, drinks and everyday essentials, making it easy for festivalgoers to pick up anything from fresh fruit, meals and cold drinks to sun cream, toiletries and toilet roll which removes the need for stocking-up pre-event and helping festivalgoers to lighten their loads as they travel from home to the campsite.
At around 6,000sq ft, each store stocks more than 300 products, giving festivalgoers access to many of the same trusted own-brand and branded favourites they’d find in their local Co-op store.
For more information, please visit: Co-op’s 2026 on-site festival stores – Co-op

Ingka Group, the largest IKEA retailer, other IKEA franchisees, and Inter IKEA Group are investing EUR 1.2 billion to lower prices across markets in Europe. These investments reinforce the company’s long-term commitment to […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
IKEA takes a big step to make home furnishing more affordable as many people continue to feel pressure from higher living costs. Ingka Group, the largest IKEA retailer, other IKEA franchisees, and Inter IKEA Group are investing EUR 1.2 billion to lower prices across markets in Europe.
These investments reinforce the company’s long-term commitment to affordable home furnishing while securing value for money through good design, quality, and sustainable choices. Rooted in the IKEA vision of creating a better everyday life, the company is lowering prices on hundreds of products to make everyday essentials and customer favourites more accessible.
“Keeping prices low is our long-term commitment and part of our promise to side with the many people,” says Juvencio Maeztu, CEO of Ingka Group | IKEA. “The investment is not an activity or short- term campaign – it’s about making IKEA more affordable when people need it most, even if it means accepting a lower margin. At the same time, we are investing to make IKEA more accessible by opening many smaller stores as part of our omnichannel experience.”
“What is unique about IKEA,” he says, “is that even while we reduce prices, quality, design, functionality, and sustainability keep increasing. This is what we call Democratic Design, and it is what enables us to offer the best value for money.”
The initiative concentrates on Europe, where prices will be cut starting from September 1. This includes popular and iconic products such as the KALLAX storage solutions, HEMNES daybed and the POÄNG armchair, with average price reductions ranging from 15% to 25%. The selection of products and price decrease will differ from market to market.
- In Germany, more than 1,500 products will have their prices lowered by an average of 20%. These include the BESTÅ TV bench, which is reduced by 27%, and IKEA 365+ kitchen products by up to 24%.
- In the UK, prices will be reduced on hundreds of home furnishing products and accessories, including the iconic BILLY bookcase by 28% and the TROFAST storage combination by 24%.
In Italy, prices on hundreds of products have been reduced by an average of 22%, including the KIVIK sofa and the POÄNG armchair.
The price reductions follow the investment made in FY24, when prices were lowered across IKEA markets for thousands of products. That investment helped more people access IKEA items and contributed to increased visitation as well as a higher number of orders.
To support affordability beyond Europe, Ingka Group will also invest EUR 70 million to help offset inflationary and currency pressures in Asia and North America, helping keep prices as low as possible for customers.

items.body:
Today, NIQ (NYSE: NIQ), a leading consumer intelligence company, and Morrisons, one of UK’s leading supermarket groups, announced a strategic collaboration designed to support market share growth across the organisation through advanced analytics, omnichannel intelligence, and actionable decision-making tools.
The collaboration brings together Morrisons’ drive to continually expand its insight capabilities with NIQ’s measurement, market intelligence, and technology ecosystem. By leveraging NIQ’s Full View™ approach, Morrisons aims to build a comprehensive understanding of market dynamics across supermarkets, online grocery, convenience and emerging retail channels, allowing teams to identify growth opportunities and act with clarity and confidence.
As retailers navigate complex consumer behaviour, connecting market signals, shopper trends, and commercial performance within a unified decision-making framework is increasingly vital. Through this collaboration, NIQ will provide Morrisons with responsive market insights, enhanced product and category intelligence, automated reporting capabilities, and self-service analytics intended to streamline workflows and support agility across the business.
Key Benefits of the Collaboration:
- Support agile decision-making through timely access to actionable market intelligence
- Maintain clear visibility across supermarkets, e-commerce, convenience, and emerging channels
- Streamline processes through automated reporting and self-service analytics
- Strengthen product attribution, category intelligence, and coding governance
- Leverage AI-enabled tools and advanced analytics to uncover new growth opportunities
“Retailers today need the ability to seamlessly turn insight into action,” said Russell Sylvester, NIQ Retail Vertical Lead UK & IRE. “By combining market measurement, consumer intelligence, omnichannel analytics, and advanced capabilities within a single ecosystem, we aim to support Morrisons in building a robust platform for future growth.”
Jen Price, customer director at Morrisons, said: “We’re excited to be launching this new collaboration with NIQ, which will deliver product and category intelligence across the full breadth of our retail channels, unlocking value through great insights and helping us make the right decisions quickly, to drive our future growth.”
The collaboration reflects a broader industry focus on connected intelligence, where retailers seek integrated solutions that unite market performance, consumer behaviour, analytics, and technology. NIQ’s combination of broad market measurement, e-commerce coverage, consumer intelligence, and AI-enabled innovation positions the company to help retailers connect data directly to commercial outcomes.
This announcement highlights the collaboration between both organisations and the role of automation and connected consumer intelligence in supporting the future of retail. Together, NIQ and Morrisons are establishing a framework designed to inform smarter decisions and support long-term performance in a dynamic marketplace.

items.title: Mike Ashley's Frasers Group eyes majority ownership of Hugo Boss as it reconsiders support for German retailer's chief
items.summary: Mike Ashley's Frasers Group is plotting to buy more shares and take majority control of Hugo Boss as it reconsiders its support for the firm's chair.
items.body:
Mike Ashley's Frasers Group eyes majority ownership of Hugo Boss as it reconsiders support for German retailer's chief
- See more This is Money on Google - save us as a Preferred Source
Mike Ashley’s Frasers Group is plotting to buy more shares and take majority control of Hugo Boss as it reconsiders its support for the firm’s chair.
The retail giant, owned by the billionaire, last month said it had increased its shareholding in the German fashion house to 47.89 per cent after recent deals to acquire extra shares.
This morning, Frasers said it intends to ‘further increase’ its ownership of Hugo Boss as it tightens its grip on the retailer just weeks after buying Harvey Nichols.
It told investors that it intends to bring its holding to above 50 per cent of the overall share capital and voting rights.
British billionaire Mike Ashley is looking to move further into the luxury market
The company also said it is reviewing whether it supports the current chair of Hugo Boss’s supervisory board, Stephan Sturm. It marks another u-turn for Frasers, which initially opposed Mr Sturm's leadership before revising its stance in June.
The FTSE 250 retailer has built its holding in Hugo Boss, which it stocks in its Flannels and Frasers shops, since its first investment in 2020, sparking speculation it would one day make a formal offer.
Ashley had reportedly been hoping to install Michael Murray, his son-in-law and Frasers boss, as chief executive of Hugo Boss.
In July, Frasers owned around 36 per cent of Hugo Boss, breaching the 30 per cent threshold after which companies are required to make a mandatory takeover bid under German takeover law.
It offered to pay around £1.7billion for the remaining shares, equivalent to €38 per share.
Hugo Boss's management and supervisory board said the deal was 'inadequate from a financial point of view' and urged shareholders to reject it.
Last month, 17.6 per cent of Hugo Boss investors tendered their shares in support of its €38 per share takeover bid bringing its stake to nearly 48 per cent.
It comes shortly after Frasers ramped up its presence in the luxury market after buying department store chain Harvey Nichols.
The £40million rescue deal came after the chain warned it would run out of money if it failed to secure new investment.
The acquisition forms part of Frasers' 'elevation strategy' aimed at increasing its presence in the luxury market, building on the growth of its Flannels brand.
However, Murray warned the deal would require 'tough choices', adding: 'We are prepared to make those decisions, even if it means a smaller business in the near term.'

items.body:
As the school gates reopen and festive planning quietly begins behind the scenes, Argos has unveiled its highly anticipated list of Top Toys for Christmas 2026. Handpicked and carefully curated by its trusted toy experts after months of market research, the lineup highlights 20 of the most-wanted gifts set to dominate letters to Santa this year.
“This year’s Top Toys list brings together the very best in imaginative play and innovation,” says Chantal Pearce, Head of Toy Buying at Argos. “We’re always monitoring market trends to discover what truly sparks children’s imaginations, and our 2026 Top Toys list reflects the toys we expect to capture their attention this Christmas. From movie magic and retro nostalgia to screen-free storytellers and hands-on crafting, we’ve curated a range that inspires imagination, supports children’s development and encourages creativity through play.”
“Toys have been at the heart of Argos for over 50 years, helping families create magical Christmas moments year after year. As a brand, generations of families have trusted our expertise on toys, and we hope to continue inspiring gift-givers this festive season.”
Throwback Favourites
Nostalgia is set to continue shaping how families shop for toys this Christmas, with classic formats getting a contemporary upgrade. Today’s retro throwbacks bridge the gap between generations, giving parents a chance to share the things they loved as children with their own kids.
“Parents enjoy introducing their children to the toys and characters they grew up with, but kids still want something that feels fresh and fun to play with,” says Chantal. “When a toy balances that retro charm with modern features, it quickly becomes a favourite across the household.”
Leading this retro revival is Mini Brands Really Works Vinyl Playset (£20) — a fully functioning mini vinyl record player that really spins and plays music from chart-topping artists, complete with 44 mini records to collect. Gaming history also makes a strong impact with the LEGO Donkey Kong Arcade Building Set (£150), bringing classic 80s arcade culture home in brick form.
Meanwhile, high-octane classic play gets scaled up in the Hot Wheels City Ultimate T-Rex Garage (£130), featuring space to store and launch up to 50 cars. Traditional wooden play also remains a firm favourite with two Argos exclusives: the Chad Valley Alfie And Jo Wooden Train Set (£15) and the Chad Valley Wooden Classic Kitchen (£30).
Future Play
Interactive technology continues to bring brilliant extra layers to everyday play, encouraging creativity, sparking curiosity and giving children exciting new ways to express themselves through music, storytelling and roleplay.
“The best interactive toys are all about instant fun and encouraging kids to dive right in,” says Chantal. “It’s wonderful seeing how intuitive tech can bring so much joy and confidence to playtime.”
A brand-new toy set to become a firm favourite this Christmas, the Tonies Lite (£60) offers a fresh update to the popular audio range. Designed as a compact, travel-friendly alternative to the Toniebox, it makes taking stories, music and audio adventures on the go easier than ever.
Meanwhile, for children who enjoy roleplay, the Little Live Pets My Magical Dragon Skye (£55) is set to be a hit. A mythical companion with over 60 physical reactions, the toy responds with sounds and movements whenever children pet, feed or play with it.
Continuing with the theme of animals and creatures, the Primal Hatch Megalodon Hatching Egg Shark Toy (£55) turns opening a new toy into an event, using a simple splash of water to trigger a fizzing, foaming reaction that lets kids “hatch” their own prehistoric shark.
Finally, clever tech features also give kids exciting ways to learn and express themselves musically. The VTech Kidi 12-In-1 Guitar Superstar (£50) uses light-up frets on the neck to guide beginners through playing real tunes, while the Projector Karaoke Machine (£90) pairs smart app connectivity with built-in stage lights so kids can put on full concerts at home.
Mini Worlds & Big Adventures
Small-world building and hands-on crafting gives children complete control over their own imaginative stories. From customising crafts to creating detailed mini setups, this trend is all about immersion—giving children space to express themselves and create their own adventures.
“Creative play gives kids the freedom to build their own stories from scratch,” says Chantal. “Whether they’re designing gifts for friends or losing themselves in an imaginative world, these toys are all about hands-on fun that keeps them engaged for hours.”
Building sets lead the charge for storytellers. LEGO Pokémon SMART Play: Sprigatito, Fuecoco and Quaxly Battle (£30) lets fans build their favourite starter Pokémon for creative play, while the Armosaurs Armor-Up Dinosaur T-Rex – Ajax (£45) brings action to life with tail-activated jaw movement and seven pieces of mix-and-match armour.
For kids who love to design and customise, the Giftie Badge Maker (£35) turns any bedroom into a crafting studio, connecting with a simple phone app to print custom photo badges and greeting cards for friends. Classic dollhouse play also gets a modern upgrade with the Argos-exclusive Jupiter Workshops Four Storey Wooden Doll House (£150), a four-story setup with working lights and sounds across contemporary styled rooms.
Finally, soft toys offer a comforting way for younger kids to process big feelings. The Argos-exclusive Flutter Monster 40 cm Soft Toy (£20) combines plush comforting cuddles with a hidden tummy pocket and feeling cards, giving children a gentle, easy way to share how they’re feeling alongside a bedtime storybook.
As Seen on Screen
Favourite TV shows and blockbuster movies continue to inspire some of the most-wanted toys under the tree. This trend is all about bringing beloved characters off the screen and into everyday play, turning iconic moments into hands-on adventures kids can lead themselves.
“When kids fall in love with a movie or show, they want to step right into that world,” says Chantal. “Screen-inspired toys are at their best when they let children recreate their favourite moments or create brand-new stories with characters they already adore.”
Leading the movie excitement is Disney’s latest blockbuster, represented by the Argos-exclusive Toy Story 5 Bullseye Jumbo Plush (£50), a super-sized, extra-huggable version of Woody’s loyal companion. Pop culture fans can also take centre stage with the KPop Demon Hunters Golden Singing Dolls (£35 each). Available in 3 styles – Rumi, Mira, and Zoey; each singing dolls performs the band’s hit song from the film, “Golden”.
For preschoolers, screen favourites come to life in a big way. The Megasaurus Dino Vehicle (£60) brings PAW Patrol: The Dino Movie to the living room with a massive 76.2cm dinosaur that automatically inflates at the press of a button. Meanwhile, Ready Pedal Peppa (£30) lets little ones help Peppa Pig learn to ride her bike with over 75 interactive sounds and phrases.
Rounding out the lineup for kids who love a good laugh, the Minions & Monsters Fart Blaster Pro (£30) lets pranksters launch real scented fart rings that float up to six feet through the air.
All 20 Top Toys and thousands more are available online at Argos.co.uk and in selected Argos stores nationwide. items.body:
The Perfume Shop, the UK’s largest specialist perfume retailer, is reinforcing its position as a market leader with the launch of the UK’s first dedicated high street Scent Rediscovery Service. As people increasingly turn to perfume as part of their wider wellbeing and self-care routines, the service is a personalised consultation designed to help customers rediscover the perfumes they love as their sense of smell, preferences and lifestyle naturally evolve over time.
The new service reflects The Perfume Shop’s continued investment in expert-led retail experiences, recognising that the relationship people have with perfume can change throughout different stages of life.
The service has been developed in response to wider shifts across the beauty and wellness market, where people are increasingly seeking products and experiences that support emotional wellbeing, confidence and self expression. New research commissioned by The Perfume Shop among 2,000 UK adults found that changes to people’s sense of smell are becoming increasingly common, with one in three (33%) attributing this to ageing, followed by illness (20%), allergies (16%), stress (15%), lifestyle changes (15%), hormonal changes (12%) and medication (12%). The findings reflect how changing wellbeing, health and life stages can reshape the way people experience perfume, prompting many to reassess the role scent plays in their daily routines.
The launch follows the same research, which found that 36% of people associate perfume with confidence, 31% linking it to feeling attractive and almost one in four (23%) viewing scent as part of their identity, the findings highlight the growing need for personalised advice to help customers rediscover perfumes that reflect who they are today.
In response to this changing consumer behaviour, the Scent Rediscovery Service offers one-to-one consultations with The Perfume Shop’s trained perfume experts. Through guided conversations around changing scent preferences, favourite fragrance families and lifestyle, customers receive tailored recommendations in a relaxed, judgement-free environment.
Following each consultation, customers leave with a personalised perfume preference providing a record of the perfumes and scent notes that best match their evolving preferences and making future perfume shopping even more personal.
The launch forms part of The Perfume Shop’s wider strategy to continue evolving the in-store customer experience through specialist expertise, personalisation and retail services that cannot be replicated online.
Karen Harris, Customer Director at The Perfume Shop, said: “At The Perfume Shop, we’ve always believed choosing a perfume is a deeply personal experience. Over time, the way we experience scent naturally changes, whether through different life stages, changing tastes or simply discovering new fragrance families that better reflect who we are.
We’re proud to be introducing the UK’s first dedicated in-store Scent Rediscovery Service. It represents another step in our commitment to delivering expert-led, personalised experiences that set our stores apart and help every customer discover, enjoy and fall back in love with perfume. The Scent Rediscovery Service has been created to give customers the confidence to explore those changes with the support of our perfume experts. Rather than simply helping someone find a new perfume, we’re helping them rediscover the joy of perfume and build a new connection with scent that feels right for them today.”
The Scent Rediscovery Service is now available in across 14 participating The Perfume Shop stores, with consultations delivered by specially trained perfume experts. The initiative reinforces The Perfume Shop’s commitment to combining more than 30 years of perfume expertise with innovative customer experiences, strengthening its position as the UK’s leading specialist perfume retailer.
The Scent Rediscovery Service is currently available at the following The Perfume Shop stores: Barnsley, Bluewater, Blanchardstown, Brent Cross, Burnley, Cardiff 2, Clydebank, Edinburgh, Enfield, Foyleside, Lakeside Upper, Merry Hill, Solihull and Trafford.

items.body:
Yorkshire supermarket chain expands its popular Food 2 Go range with affordable hot meals, snacks and drinks for school lunches and after-school dinners.
As thousands of children head back to school this September, Leeds-based Abu Bakr Supermarket has unveiled a brand-new range of affordable kids’ meals, with prices starting from just £1.50.
The new menu will be available from the Food 2 Go counters in every Abu Bakr Supermarket store across Leeds and Batley, with the family-run retailer saying the range has been created to offer quick, filling and value-for-money options for busy parents and schoolchildren alike.
The offer starts at just £1.50, with customers able to pick up two freshly made samosas for only £1.50 or a hot pasty for £1.50, making it one of the supermarket’s most affordable freshly prepared food ranges for families.
The launch builds on Abu Bakr’s growing Food 2 Go brand, which has become one of the supermarket chain’s fastest-growing fresh food offerings.
The new school meal range includes:
| Meal | Price | 
| Two freshly made samosas (including vegetarian options) | £1.50 | 
| One hot pasty (including vegetarian options) | £1.50 | 
| Butter Chicken or Chicken Tikka Masala, with a choice of meat and vegetarian curry alternatives | £7.50 | 
| Freshly made warm naan bread | £1.00 | 
| Two cans of Coke or a selection of fresh juice drinks | £1.00 | 
The meals have been designed so customers can mix and match snacks, drinks and hot food, making the range ideal for school lunches, after-school meals or an affordable family dinner.
Abu Bakr Supermarket says the launch comes at a time when many parents are looking for affordable food options during the expensive back-to-school period.
Managing director Hamza Hussain said the retailer wanted to combine convenience with quality while keeping prices accessible.
“Back to school is one of the busiest and most expensive times of the year for families, so we wanted Food 2 Go to offer something that’s fresh, filling and genuinely affordable.
“Our new kids meal range has been created for busy parents and hungry children who want quality food without paying takeaway prices. Whether it’s a couple of samosas after school, a hot pasty on the go, or a Butter Chicken or Chicken Tikka Masala that the family can enjoy at home, we’ve made sure there’s something for everyone and every budget.
“The best part is that every single Abu Bakr store will now offer these meals through our Food 2 Go counters, giving customers the same great choice wherever they shop.”
The Food 2 Go counters are already a popular feature inside Abu Bakr Supermarkets, serving freshly prepared halal meals, bakery items, sandwiches and hot food throughout the day.
The new kids meal range will be available across Abu Bakr Supermarket stores in Queens Road, Roundhay Road, Dewsbury Road, Kirkstall Road and Batley, ensuring customers can enjoy the same freshly prepared Food 2 Go menu at every location.
With Abu Bakr continuing its rapid expansion across Yorkshire, the supermarket says Food 2 Go will remain a major part of its investment in affordable, freshly prepared meals for local communities.

Trading cards continue to be a major growth area for eBay, with […] If you want more information Retail Times get in touch! Retail Times - Retail Times, a free to view retail news website
items.body:
eBay, the world’s largest online marketplace for trading cards, today announced the expansion of its new trading card price guide to the UK. eBay is the first online marketplace in the UK to offer collectors a dedicated price guide for trading card games.
Trading cards continue to be a major growth area for eBay, with collectables remaining the largest contributor to the company’s global GMV growth in Q2 2026.1 Values can vary by condition, grade and demand, so access to up-to-date pricing and market data can help collectors and enthusiasts make more informed decisions when buying and selling.
With the latest version of the eBay app, collectors can access the new eBay price guide and scan cards from popular trading card games including Pokémon, Magic: The Gathering, Yu-Gi-Oh!, One Piece and Disney Lorcana to instantly view recent eBay sales data and help track the value of their collections. Price guide insights will also be available across the eBay app and desktop as the experience rolls out, including directly from trading card listings by
selecting ‘See insights’. Supporting both raw and selected graded trading card singles, the price guide draws on up to two years of completed transactions on eBay.co.uk.
The launch comes during a significant year for the trading card community. With Pokémon celebrating its 30th anniversary, MCM Comic Con drawing thousands of fans, and a packed calendar of new product releases, the trading card hobby is growing and attracting a wider fan base. In July 2026 alone, “Pokémon” was searched more than six million times on eBay.co.uk, underlining the continued interest in trading card collecting across the UK.
Adam Ireland, Vice President and General Manager, Global Collectables at eBay commented, “We’re continuing to invest in our trading card business and support our dedicated community of buyers and sellers with innovations that streamline the shopping experience. Earlier this year, we launched Authenticity Guarantee for trading cards in the UK. Now, we’re putting even more information in collector’s hands with eBay’s price guide, making it easier than ever for seasoned collectors and new enthusiasts to participate in the fast-paced trading card hobby.”
Recent activity on eBay.co.uk illustrates the pace of the market, with searches for One Piece rising 55% month-on-month ahead of the second season of Netflix’s live-action adaptation.
How price guide works:
Collectors can access the eBay price guide through the latest version of the eBay app by navigating to My eBay and selecting “Scan cards” from the Shortcuts menu.
● Scan and identify: Scan raw or selected graded trading cards using a smartphone camera to quickly identify cards and find relevant comparables.
● Access recent sales data: View up to two years of first-party eBay sales data, including accepted Best Offer prices, updated within the last 24 hours.
● Compare: Toggle between sold and active listings and view PSA and CGC population report data to better understand market value and rarity.
● Free to use: Available to UK eBay account holders on the latest version of the eBay app, with no subscription fees or usage limits. Availability will roll out from 1 September 2026.

Pokémon
● eBay.co.uk users searched for “Pokémon” more than 105 times per minute on average in 2025.
● In March 2026, as Pokémon celebrated its 30th anniversary alongside a slate of new trading card releases, a 2000 Pokémon Gym Challenge 1st Edition Booster Box sold for £37,000 in April 2026.
Magic: The Gathering
● A serialised The One Ring (79/100) card sold for £19,850 in January 2025.
One Piece
● In January 2026, as anticipation built towards the second season of Netflix’s live-action One Piece, searches for “One Piece” on eBay.co.uk increased by 55% compared to the month prior (December 2025).

items.title: Shein shares slide on fast-fashion retailer’s stock market debut
items.summary: Hong Kong flotation at $26bn by firm once valued at $100bn follows failure to list in US and UK Shares in the fast-fashion brand Shein slumped as much as 10% as the China-founded company made its long-anticipated trading debut on the Hong Kong stock exchange. The Singapore-headquartered company, once valued at almost $100bn (£74bn), went public on Tuesday pricing shares at HK$48.56, valuing the business at just over $26bn. Continue reading...
items.body:
Shares in the fast-fashion brand Shein slumped as much as 10% as the China-founded company made its long-anticipated trading debut on the Hong Kong stock exchange.
The Singapore-headquartered company, once valued at almost $100bn (£74bn), went public on Tuesday pricing shares at HK$48.56, valuing the business at just over $26bn.
However, minutes after the flotation, which raised HK$13.6bn, the stock fell as much as 10%, pushing the online retailer’s valuation below $25bn. Shein’s share price recovered some ground to be 4% below its offer price by the end of trading, at HK$46.62.
“Let global consumers enjoy the sound of fashion,” said Leigh Gui, Shein’s chief financial officer, after a gong was struck to mark the start of trading.
The lacklustre launch as a publicly listed company comes after one of the longest-awaited initial public offerings in recent years, after plans to list in New York were blocked by regulators over forced labour concerns.
Shein also considered a £50bn flotation in London but faced similar questions about its supply chain from campaigners, MPs and investors.
The plunge in value has been driven by regulatory changes around the world that threaten its business model of shipping goods in small packages out of China to take advantage of tax breaks on low-value imported goods.
Shein swung to a loss of $99m in the first three months of this year, compared with a net income of $395m the year before, after the US removed its “de minimis” import duty exemption on small packages, hitting its sales in the country.
The EU is also cracking down on the loophole – introducing a €3 (£2.56) duty on small parcels imported from outside the trading bloc in June – and intends to phase it out, while the UK has said it will do the same by October 2028.
Nevertheless, the company has still become one of the world’s biggest listed fashion groups, with a valuation around the same as the Swedish retailer H&M. The Zara owner, Inditex, has a market capitalisation of about $213bn.
Shein moved its headquarters to Singapore at about the start of 2022, a move viewed by analysts as designed to avoid increasing scrutiny of Chinese companies.
Founded by the entrepreneur Chris Xu, the company runs most of its operations from China but sells all its goods outside the country. It reached a valuation of $100bn in an April 2022 fundraising round, making it the third most valuable startup in the world at the time.
After forced labour concerns were raised, Shein said it had tightened its supplier policies, enforced through regular audits, with any child or forced labour violations becoming grounds for immediate termination of contract.

items.title: Mike Ashley’s Frasers weighs move to oust Hugo Boss chief
items.summary: Mike Ashley’s Frasers Group is weighing up a move to oust a boardroom chair at Hugo Boss as it laid out fresh plans to grow its stake in the German fashion house. The retail group, which was founded by the British billionaire, told investors on Tuesday that it wants to control more than half of [...]
items.body:
Mike Ashley’s Frasers weighs move to oust Hugo Boss chief
Mike Ashley’s Frasers Group is weighing up a move to oust a boardroom chair at Hugo Boss as it laid out fresh plans to grow its stake in the German fashion house.
The retail group, which was founded by the British billionaire, told investors on Tuesday that it wants to control more than half of Hugo Boss. It already owns nearly 48 per cent of the group, making it its biggest shareholder.
Frasers Group’s update cast doubt on the position of Stephan Sturm as the chairman of Hugo Boss’s supervisory board, suggesting it could launch a coup against him.
The group said: “Frasers is currently reviewing whether it continues to support Mr. Stephan Sturm in his position as the Chairman of the Supervisory Board of Hugo Boss.”
A potential bid to replace Sturm would be the latest in Frasers’s long history of boardroom bust-ups. The group has garnered a reputation for taking stakes in rival companies and using these positions to make aggressive plays for change within the firm.
Sturm has been chair of Hugo Boss’s supervisory board since May last year. Michael Murray, chief executive of Frasers, holds a seat on the board.
Hugo Boss’s supervisory board sits above its managing board, scrutinising its work and appointing the members of this panel.
Frasers pushes into luxury fashion
Last month, Frasers upped its stake in the German fashion house to 47.9 per cent – a holding worth nearly €1.5bn.
Frasers had tabled a £1.7bn offer for the entire group, but this was slapped down as “inadequate” by Hugo Boss. The UK group instead appealed to investors, picking up about 17 per cent of Hugo Boss with its €38-per-share offer.
Frasers has reportedly been pushing to install Murray, who is Ashley’s son-in-law, as chief executive of Hugo Boss.
In 2024, Frasers built up stakes in luxury bagmaker Mulberry and online retailer Boohoo, but failed in its attempts to gain seats on the boards of both companies.
Earlier this year, Ashley launched a £166m takeover bid for Australian shoe company Accent and called for the removal of its chairman over his alleged “poor performance”.
The group’s pursuit of Hugo Boss comes as Ashley, who founded Sports Direct, seeks to push his retail empire upmarket.
Last month, Frasers bought struggling department store chain Harvey Nichols out of administration for about £40m.
The group, which also owns up-market brand Flannels, said its acquisition of Harvey Nichols will build on its “elevation strategy, strengthening its luxury positioning”.
Ashley founded Frasers Group in 1982. Its slate of brands includes Jack Wills, Evans Cycles, Lonsdale and Slazenger.

items.title: Shop prices rising at fastest pace in more than two years
items.summary: Shop prices are rising at their fastest pace in more than two years adding to the cost of living pressure squeezing UK households.
items.body:
Shop prices rising at fastest pace in more than two years
- See more This is Money on Google - save us as a Preferred Source
Shop prices are rising at their fastest pace in more than two years adding to the cost of living pressure squeezing UK households.
The British Retail Consortium (BRC) said prices rose by 1.5 per cent last month, up from 0.9 per cent the month before and the highest since February 2024.
It comes as consumers are already being hit by a series of increases in energy bills – and threatens to derail Andy Burnham’s ambitions to ease the burden on household finances.
The BRC’s shop price index is a narrower gauge than official inflation figures, which cover a wider basket of goods and services.
Shop prices rose by 1.5% in August, the fastest pace since February 2024
But its rise is still likely to add to concerns that hard-working families will be finding it tougher to make ends meet – leaving them less likely to splash out beyond the essentials.
BRC chief executive Helen Dickinson said: ‘The months ahead look challenging for households, with rising bills putting further pressure on budgets.’
She said soaring operating costs for retailers meant it was harder for them to keep prices in check without affecting investment and jobs.
It comes at a time when firms are being hammered by higher employer national insurance, rising minimum wages and botched business rates reform.
‘If the Government is serious about supporting growth while keeping the cost of living in check, it must address the cost of doing business, including by tackling the growing burden of business rates, packaging and employment taxes,’ Dickinson said.
The BRC’s figures showed non-food inflation rose sharply from 0.2 per cent in July to 0.9 per cent in August, the highest since February 2024.
And food inflation climbed from 2.2 per cent to 2.8 per cent, the highest since April this year.
Dickinson said the impact of higher energy and commodity costs on firms were ‘beginning to filter through into prices’.
This was particularly true of so-called ‘ambient’ foods that can be stored at room temperature such as tinned goods or breakfast cereal, which are typically imported and processed, adding cost.
Meanwhile, electrical prices are rising because the artificial intelligence (AI) boom is forcing up the price of memory chips and storage, Dickinson added.
Wider inflation is rising because of Donald Trump’s Iran war, which has choked off oil and gas supplies from the Middle East.
That has notably pushed up energy prices, with regulator Ofgem announcing last week that the cap on household energy bills will rise by 4 per cent from October to a three-year high and forecasters predicting a further 9 per cent hike in January.

items.body:
FTSE 100 Live: Stocks drop; Oil jumps as Trump vows more strikes on Iran
Welcome back to the City AM liveblog.
The London market is returning from the Bank Holiday break to a fall as tensions in the Middle East are simmering over again leading to the price of oil moving higher.
Brent crude – the international benchmark for oil prices – climbed over $91 per barrel on Tuesday, extending gains from the previous session as the renewal of strike action in the Middle East raised concerns about further disruptions to energy flows from the region.
It follows the US launching strikes at Iranian rocket launchers that were reportedly preparing to lay mines in the Strait of Hormuz, marking the first exchange of fire in more than a month. Since then, Iran has responded targeting US military bases in Jordan and the United Arab Emirates.
Achilleas Georgolopoulos, senior market analyst at Trading Point, said fresh military operations were pushing the oil price higher. But he added the rally appeared to “lack [the] momentum” needed to push it above previous highs seen during the conflict.
“While no one is surprised by these events, expectations for progress in the US-Oman-Iran negotiations have clearly taken another hit,” he added.
The White House last week signalled that it was shelving military measures in favour of a method to destroy the Iranian economy through enforcing sanctions.
But Trump has suggested military action is back on the table after Iran’s retaliation.
“We’re going to hit them hard. There will be a response.” Trump told Fox News. He also branded Iran “officially a failed nation without an airforce, a navy or a currency”.
We’ll be bringing you the latest market updates and analysis.

The awards are now open for entries and celebrate global retail technology innovation in a fast moving omnichannel world.
Our winners will be revealed at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London on Wednesday, 4th November.
Check out our 2025 winners here.

Kurt Miller announces departure from QVC Group and takes on Head of Fulfillment Excellence position at Wayfair
Kurt Miller has joined Wayfair as Head of Fulfilment Excellence. He was previously Director of Engineering & Process Optimisation and has also worked at Amazon and PKC Group. In a LinkedIn post, he said: "As I begin this next chapter, I’ve spent a lot of time reflecting on an incredible five-year journey with QVC, where I had the privilege of leading the Engineering and Operational Excellence team."
"I am incredibly grateful for the opportunity to have worked alongside so many talented individuals throughout my time at QVC. Together, we navigated challenges, drove meaningful improvements, built strong teams, and accomplished things I will remain proud of for years to come.”
He added: "More importantly, I leave with friendships, lessons, and memories that extend far beyond the work itself. To the colleagues, leaders, and team members who were part of that journey - thank you. Your partnership, support, and commitment made these past five years incredibly rewarding, and I will always appreciate my time at QVC."
"I’m now looking forward to this next chapter with Wayfair and the opportunity to lead fulfilment excellence. I’m excited to work alongside another talented organisation as we continue advancing operational excellence, process innovation, and the future of fulfillment. Grateful for the journey behind me and energised for what’s ahead!"
2026 RTIH Innovation Awards
Fulfilment excellence will be a key focus area at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards.
The awards are now open for entries and celebrate global retail technology innovation in a fast moving omnichannel world.
Our winners will be revealed at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London on Wednesday, 4th November.
Check out our 2025 winners here.
Our 2025 hall of fame entrants were revealed during a sold out event which took place at The HAC on 16th October and consisted of a drinks reception, three course meal, and awards ceremony presided over by award winning comedian, actress and writer Tiff Stevenson.
In his welcome speech, Scott Thompson, Founder and Editor, RTIH, said: “This is the awards’ fifth year as a physical event. We started off with just 30 people at the South Place Hotel not far from here, then moved to London Bridge Hotel, then The Barbican, and last year RIBA’s HQ in the West End.”
“But I’m conscious of the fact that, to quote the legend that is Taylor Swift, You’re only as hot as your last hit, baby. So, this year we’ve moved to our biggest venue yet, and also pulled in our largest number of entries to date and broken attendance records.”
He added: “This year’s submissions have without doubt been our best yet. To quote one of the judges: The examples of innovative developments across both traditional and digital retail spaces were truly remarkable.”
Congratulations to our winners, and a big thank you to our sponsors, judging panel, the legend that is Tiff Stevenson, and all those who attended our 2025 gathering.
Editor and Founder of Retail Technology Innovation Hub

Gerri Martin-Flickinger, formerly EVP, Chief Technology Officer at Starbucks, has joined the board of directors at Victoria's Secret.
In a LinkedIn post, she said: "I've spent much of my career helping organisations navigate change, embrace innovation, and leverage technology to create stronger customer experiences and business outcomes. I'm looking forward to bringing that perspective to the VS&Co board as the company advances its Path to Potential strategy and continues shaping its next chapter."
"VS&Co is at an important point in its journey, and I look forward to working alongside the board and leadership team to help create long-term value."
Andrew Corner
Starbucks has appointed Andrew Corner as Senior Vice President of Supply Chain. He joins from Nike where he spent almost ten years, most recently serving as VP of Global Supply Chain & Planning Operations.
He said: “Ten years. That's how long I've called Nike home, and it's hard to put into words what that decade has meant to me. I joined as someone who loved sport. I'm leaving as someone who got to help move it. Nike gave me room to grow and work that mattered, but what I'll really carry with me are the people. The teams who showed up for each other on the hardest days, the mentors who took a chance on me before I'd earned it, and the friendships that will long outlast any chapter. To my Nike family: thank you! You shaped who I am, professionally and otherwise. I'll be cheering you on from the sidelines, loudly!”
He added: “And now, a new chapter. I'm thrilled to share that I'm joining Starbucks as SVP of Supply Chain. Here's what I keep coming back to. Not everyone gets to work for a company they genuinely love. I've now been lucky enough to do it twice. Sport and coffee, two things that were part of my life long before they were part of my job. I don't take that for granted for a second. To my new Starbucks partners: I can't wait to get started.”

items.body:
High profile exits and hires at lulelemon and Target: the biggest retail technology stories from August
August is done and dusted, September is up and running, so let’s kick back and reflect on another eventful month for the retail technology space. Here's your briefing on the most important stories from August, including Walmart, Tesco, Simbe, Everseen, Morrisons, Asda, Auror, Sainsbury's, Facewatch, AutoStore, Amazon, Everseen, Hanshow, OpenAI, and Ikea UK.
1. Walmart backs down on stand against contactless payments with Apple and Google Pay
Walmart is adding tap to pay options to its checkout stations at US stores and Sam's Club warehouses, with deployment set for completion by end of year. Fuel stations will be upgraded by mid-2027. This includes options like Apple Pay and Google Pay.
Walmart has long resisted the rise and rise of NFC-based payments, opting instead to go all in on its Walmart Pay app and Scan and Go app features for contactless payments.
In a LinkedIn post, Sam Amrani, Founder and CEO at PassBy, said: "Isn't it crazy to think that it's 2026 and Walmart doesn't accept Apple Pay? Until now that is. This has been a case of America's largest retailer vs America's largest consumer tech company."
He added: "Inevitably, Walmart Pay will go down as the largest attempt at creating a closed loop payment system. Its demise will be the final nail in the coffin for retailers trying to create proprietary payment rails for their ecosystem. Ultimately, convenience wins."
"The consumer is the kingmaker, and the result was clear, the convenience of Apple Pay was too important to the customer journey. It will make customers happier and Walmart - although adopting reluctantly - will see this lead to faster transaction times, happier customers and more visits."
2. Everseen, Hanshow and OpenAI top first ever RTIH Retail Technology Hot 100 List
In partnership with 3D Cloud, RTIH is pleased to launch its first ever Retail Technology Hot 100 List. We’re bringing you the hottest companies whose solutions and systems are helping drive the retail sector forward.
These companies operate across the omnichannel retail landscape (stores, online, mobile, supply chain, payments etc).
Our judging panel, including Vineta Bajaj, Group CFO, Holland & Barrett, Dan McGrath, JD Group Customer Operations, JD Sports, Dr. Astha Purohit, Director of Product Management, Customer Data and Identity, Walmart, and Paula Bobbett, Chief Data and Digital Officer, Boots, provided feedback on those who have the most innovative, forward thinking technology offerings and are also best addressing retailers' current challenges, painpoints, and opportunities.
The judges used the following framework when making their picks:
1. Retailer problem fit - how meaningful, strategic, and widely felt the retailer pain being addressed is.
2. Production traction in retail (2025–2026) - real named retailer deployments, pilots. 
3. Innovation and defensibility - genuine technical novelty paired with a defensible competitive position. 
And there was also a public vote, with thousands of members of our community of retail tech enthusiasts getting involved. Thanks to all those who took part! Based on the judging panel's feedback and the public vote, we then drew up our first ever RTIH Retail Technology Hot 100.
So, without further ado, here are the 100 hottest global retail technology ventures right now. Drum roll, please…
3. Search on for new leader as lululemon Chief AI and Technology Officer Ranju Das leaves retailer
Ranju Das has left lululemon, where he served as Chief AI and Technology Officer. He joined the retailer in September of last year, with a focus on leveraging AI and technology to redefine the retail landscape, enhancing guest experiences and internal operations.
His LinkedIn bio noted: "My role involves creating responsible AI strategies that not only improves efficiency but also adds significant value for shareholders. I work closely with diverse teams to ensure our innovation is aligned with the company’s mission of being a leading brand for people around the world who want to live a healthy and active lifestyle."
“Ranju Das has left lululemon. We are grateful for his contributions and wish him well in his next chapter,” a lululemon spokesperson told RTIH “We are conducting a global search for our next technology leader and have full confidence in our current technology teams to continue delivering on our priorities.”
The spokesperson did not reveal why Das was suddenly leaving or whether this was connected to the recent departure of Chief Strategy Officer Rachel Acheson. He exits stage left just a month before incoming Chief Heidi O’Neill is set to start.
4. Ikea UK preps launch of secondhand products marketplace following Norway and Spain pilots
Ikea UK reports the upcoming launch of a new platform: the Ikea secondhand marketplace. Available to Family members, this is a dedicated space where pre-loved products can find a new home. The platform will enable customers to connect directly with one another. The announcement builds on pilots in Spain and Norway.
An Ikea spokeperson says: “We are always looking for new ways to make life at home even better and help our customers discover products they love. With the launch of Ikea secondhand marketplace in the UK, we’re taking a meaningful step toward creating a destination that simplifies access to pre-owned Ikea furniture.”
“Our goal is to make passing on beloved Ikea pieces as seamless as possible. We’re creating a trusted and vibrant space to make it quick and easy for our Ikea Family members to trade directly with one another. We want the process for buying and selling pre-owned products to be simple, accessible and rewarding.”
Further information regarding the official launch and how customers can participate will be made available in the coming months.
5. Sainsbury's keeps the faith with Facewatch technology as customer is wrongly accused of shoplifting
Sainsbury's plans to continue with its roll-out of Facewatch facial recognition technology to approximately 200 stores during 2026, despite a customer being wrongly challenged as a shoplifter and asked to leave a store earlier this month.
A Sainsbury's spokesperson said that this resulted from human error rather than a false match by the Facewatch system and that the retailer contacted the customer to apologise for his experience. "The incident was caused by human error, not the facial recognition technology. Customers can be reassured that the Facewatch system has a 99.98% accuracy rate, and every match is reviewed by a trained manager,” they added.
A Facewatch spokesperson commented: "We can confirm that our live facial recognition technology was not at fault in this incident. A correct alert was sent to the retailer, but was subsequently subject to human error in the way it was handled and communicated by the retailer."
Matt Arnold, 46, was buying items at a Sainsbury’s store in East Dulwich when he was stopped by management at a self-service checkout. He was waiting for a staff member to approve an alcohol purchase. Having scanned his items alongside his Nectar loyalty card, he waved an attendant over, but was instead approached by management.
"They came over and said I had to leave. The staff member said I'd been identified by the AI, and the cameras had flagged me," he told BBC London. "A shoplifter does not walk around with that much shopping, they don't scan it through, they don't put their Nectar card through. But what upset me was thinking this is what the future could be - people just listen to what the machine tells them to do without thinking about the consequences."
After being escorted off the premises, Arnold said he had looked back from the entrance and saw an overhead CCTV monitor alert with a red circle surrounding his face.
6. AutoStore announces deal with Amazon to supply automation technology products and solutions
There has been a lot of chatter this year about AutoStore and Amazon, the result of a jobs posting by the latter seeking staff with experience of the former. And now we have an official announcement.
The pair have shaken hands on an agreement that establishes a framework for the supply of AutoStore’s products and solutions to Amazon on a global basis. Whilst the agreement defines the terms for further procurement of AutoStore systems by Amazon, it does not contain any purchasing commitments at this time, a press release notes.
While this will no doubt boost AutoStore's share price, it should be noted that Amazon has announced similar agreements in the past, for example with Balyo, which did not result in significant sales. Balyo was taken private in 2026 by SoftBank Group Corp. which also remains a significant shareholder in AutoStore (and various others).
7. Target raids Lowe's Companies to bring in Chandhu Nair as its first ever Chief AI Officer
Chandhu Nair is joining Target as Chief AI Officer, following a six and a half year stint at Lowe’s Companies (where he most recently served as Senior Vice President - Stores, Data, AI & Innovation).
In a LinkedIn post, he said: “While spending some time in New York with my boys, we stopped by Target’s SoHo store. Watching them explore - and seeing one of them immediately gravitate toward Bullseye - was a small but meaningful reminder of what makes retail special. The brands we build become part of people’s everyday lives, their families, and their experiences.”
He added: “I’ve always believed that some of the best technology conversations happen in stores, not conference rooms. And as AI reshapes retail, its true impact won’t ultimately be measured by models, benchmarks, or the sophistication of the technology. It will be measured on the frontlines. In how we make experiences better for guests. How we empower team members. How we simplify work. And ultimately, how we make the entire enterprise smarter while keeping people at the centre. That’s what makes this opportunity so exciting.”
Nair concluded: “Target is an iconic retailer with an extraordinary brand, a deep connection with its guests, and a long history of bringing together design, technology, and human experience in distinctive ways. I’m grateful for the opportunity to partner with Prat Vemana (EVP Chief Information and Product Officer), the Target tech team and the broader leadership team as we explore what’s possible with AI and help shape the next chapter of this remarkable company. For now, I’m enjoying a little more time with my family before getting started. Can’t wait.”
8. Asda announces pilot across London stores of Auror crime reporting and intelligence technology
Asda is rolling out Auror, a crime reporting and intelligence platform. It says that a ten-week pilot in 30 London stores demonstrated the value of having a faster, more effective way to report incidents and identify repeat offenders in real-time.
According to the UK grocery retailer, the trial resulted in: more than £100,000 of products recovered and returned to shelves; 55% increase in crime prevention rates; 80% reduction in incident reporting time, from around 25 minutes to under five; improved identification of repeat and cross retailer offenders.
David Lepley, Chief Operating Officer at Asda, says: “Rolling out Auror across our estate will further strengthen our ability to prevent and tackle retail crime. The results from our London pilot demonstrated the value of having a faster and more effective way to report incidents and identify repeat offenders in real-time. By working more closely with police and retailers through a shared intelligence network, we can focus our efforts where they will have the greatest impact and help to tackle retail crime.”
9. Morrisons announces roll-out of Everseen computer vision powered Evercheck platform across stores
Morrisons has selected Everseen to deploy its Evercheck solution across 200 of the UK grocery retailer’s stores in an initial roll-out phase. The platform uses real-time computer vision to simplify the self-checkout process.
The move builds on a trial of the technology. On-screen prompts allow shoppers to correct any missed items themselves, with the aim of keeping queues moving. The software integrates with existing systems, freeing store teams to focus on customer service.
Francesca Bezoari, Store Support Office Director at Morrisons, says: “Our new partnership with Everseen enables us to provide the fast and seamless checkout experience our customers want, while simultaneously equipping our colleagues to maintain the exceptional service that Morrisons is known for.”
Joe White, CEO at Everseen, says: “Morrisons recognise that the best AI solutions deliver measurable results without compromising the customer experience. Our Vision AI platform enables Morrisons to improve its satisfaction scores, proving that operational performance and customer service aren't competing priorities. We're proud to bring our experience from deploying across thousands of global checkouts to support Morrisons transformation.”
10. Tesco extends its UK trial of Simbe's in-store autonomous inventory scanning solution Tally
In July, we reported that Tesco was trialling Simbe’s Tally in-store shelf scanning robot.
Having kicked off with a single store, the pilot is now being extended to a small number of other locations. Thanks to Toby Pickard, Retail Futures Senior Partner at IGD, and a member of the judging panel for the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards, for bringing this to our attention.
In a LinkedIn post, he said: “I’ve now seen Simbe’s Tally robot in a third Tesco store in the UK - another store trialling autonomous inventory scanning. But this time, I had my son with me. His reaction was fascinating. He was completely intrigued by Tally: watching it move around the store, trying to work out what it was doing, and following it with the kind of curiosity only a child can bring to something that feels like it has just stepped out of the future.”
He added: “I’ve heard that in the US, some shoppers will even choose stores specifically because they have Tally, because their children love seeing the robot. Honestly, I can believe it. And it got me thinking…We often talk about retail automation in terms of efficiency, accuracy, labour productivity and ROI. But what happens when the technology itself becomes part of the customer experience? Could robots like Tally become something that customers - and especially children - actively want to see?”
Could, Pickard asked, the presence of robots change which stores people choose to visit? And perhaps more importantly: what happens when the next generation grows up thinking autonomous robots moving around a supermarket is completely normal? Will they see Tally as technology? Or simply as part of what a modern store is?
Pickard concluded: “There’s a fascinating intersection here between automation, operations, customer experience and the psychology of physical retail. I’m increasingly convinced that the question isn’t just, what can robots do for retailers? It’s also, what can robots make customers feel about the future of retail?”

A campaign built on something we could all do a little more of: giving compliments.”
Highlights include: 29 million views on social media; Millions of compliments sparked; Various interactions generated; 99% positive sentiment.
Anderson added: “They say a compliment goes a long way. But who knew a "Love that" could travel quite so far? And the metric I'm most proud of isn't on this list, it's the fact that we've helped create millions of moments where someone felt appreciated, praised, admired. Love your dress. Love how that blazer elevates your whole outfit. Love those heels with that skirt. Love this whole look.”
“A compliment is never just a compliment. It's a confidence boost. A conversation starter. A little nudge to try something new. And it's always a gateway to hearing:
"Thanks, it's M&S." Together, we've sparked millions of compliments, inspired thousands of those moments and turned more heads than we could possibly count. Love that for us.”

items.title: Milestone for pop culture and lifestyle brand Miniso in USA as it opens 400th store Stateside
items.summary: Miniso, a Chinese retailer perhaps best known for its blind boxes, has opened its 400th store in America as the brand taps into the demand among US consumers for experiential in-person shopping experiences. In a LinkedIn post, Tom Bartlebaugh, CEO, Miniso USA, said: "400 and counting......Amazing team work. Amazing collaboration. So proud of the entire team." UK Miniso recently opened its latest UK store at Bristol’s Cribbs Mall. Saad Usman, Chief Operating Officer, said: “Opening at Cribbs Causeway is an exciting step for us as we continue to expand our presence nationwide. Cribbs’ dynamic and fast growing customer base makes it the ideal location for our next store, and we’re delighted to bring our fun, pop culture products to such a vibrant retail destination. We’ve created a joyful, imaginative space designed to appeal to Gen Z and Alpha, while also welcoming Millennial families, and we can’t wait to welcome shoppers through our doors.”
